zh: 在勃列日涅夫、柯西金和苏斯洛夫治下十八年的温和斯大林主义之后，苏联制度的结构性缺陷再次把改革共产主义推到前台。发起这一轮新的自上而下行动的任务落到了米哈伊尔·戈尔巴乔夫身上；而在他掌权期间，东方和西方大多数观察家都把他视为一个肩负历史使命的人——确实是一个“奇迹”——运动的开始和结果都取决于他。但把历史的复杂性人格化为“好人”戈尔巴乔夫，与把它人格化为“坏人”斯大林一样简单化。最后一位总书记和第一位总书记一样，都必须放在各自的历史背景中理解。
en: After the eighteen years of soft Stalinism under Brezhnev, Kosygin, and Suslov, the structural defects of the Soviet system once again brought Reform Communism to the fore. It fell to Mikhail Gorbachev to initiate this new round of activism from above; and while he was in power, most observers, in the East as well as in the West, saw him as a man of destiny—indeed a “miracle”—on whom both the start of the movement and its outcome depended. But to personify the complexities of history in the “good man” Gorbachev is just as simplistic as personifying them in the “bad man” Stalin. The last General Secretary, like the first, must be situated in his context.

zh: 诚然，鉴于苏联制度的性质，变革的冲动只能来自最高层。但这并不改变戈尔巴乔夫的改革，即“重建”，体现了制度长期逻辑的事实：强硬共产主义与温和共产主义之间、战时共产主义与新经济政策之间的摆动，需要周期性地出现，以便让国家为下一轮社会主义发力恢复力量。然而这一次，出乎意料，这出循环戏剧第二幕的重演，让这出此时已破旧不堪的戏永久落幕了。
en: To be sure, given the nature of Soviet institutions, the impulse for change could have come only from the top. But this does not make Gorbachev’s

, or “restructuring,” any less an expression of the long-term logic of the system: the oscillation between hard and soft Communism, between War Communism and the NEP, was periodically necessary to permit the country to recoup its strength for the next round of socialist exertion. Yet on this occasion, quite unexpectedly, the reprise of Act II of the recurring drama brought the curtain down for good on what was by now a threadbare show.

zh: 的确，共产主义退出历史的方式，比任何其他事情都更让世界惊讶。戈尔巴乔夫继承了一个超级大国和一个拥有一千九百万党员的党，两者都充满战斗性，几十年来一直让外部世界恐惧。然而掌权六年后——与列宁建立苏维埃国家所需的时间相同——戈尔巴乔夫眼看着党和联盟在他脚下解体。而且，它们消失时没有进行丝毫抵抗，更没有引发人们可能从如此庞大的力量中预期的那种震荡。苏联制度在末期异常脆弱的原因，无疑将构成未来改革史学的核心问题。
en: Indeed, nothing about Communism astonished the world as much as the manner of its exit from history. Gorbachev inherited a superpower and a nineteen-million-member Party, each bristling with a militancy that had frightened the outside world for decades. Yet after six years in power—the same span of time it took Lenin to launch the Soviet state—Gorbachev saw both the Party and the Union dissolve beneath him. They disappeared, moreover, without offering the slightest resistance, still less without giving rise to the convulsions one might expect from such imposing forces. The reasons for the extraordinary fragility of the Soviet system at its end will no doubt constitute the central question in the future historiography of

zh: 这种脆弱性的一个原因在于，第二次改革共产主义的尝试尽管表面相似，却只能与第一次有重大不同，恰恰因为第二次试图改革的结构已被前一次努力所侵蚀。勃列日涅夫之流的松软官名录共产主义不是斯大林的恐怖共产主义，末期拥有众多党员的党也不是建设社会主义的狂热队伍。将要执行新改革的一代，也与尝试第一次改革的一代不同。赫鲁晓夫改革的领导人是由斯大林制度塑造的：他们既被它吓倒，又与它的成就紧密相连；其中一些人因改革风险而清醒过来，后来就成了勃列日涅夫一代。但戈尔巴乔夫改革的领导人是在赫鲁晓夫解冻中、在他们充满希望的二十多岁时被塑造的；当退守成为必要时，他们退居的地方不过是中央委员会或科学院研究所里的舒适职位。
en: One cause of this fragility was that the second attempt at Reform Communism, despite surface appearances, could only be significantly different from the first, precisely because the structures the second sought to reform had been undermined by the preceding effort. The flaccid

Communism of Brezhnev and Co. was not the terroristic Communism of Stalin, and the multitudinous Party of the last days was not the zealous band that had built socialism. Nor was the generation that would carry out the new reform the same as that which had attempted the first. The leaders of the Khrushchev reform had been molded by the Stalin system: they were both terrified by it and wedded to its accomplishments; and some of these same men, sobered by the risks of reform, then became the Brezhnev generation. But the leaders of the Gorbachev reform had been molded by the Khrushchev thaw while they were in their hopeful twenties; and when retrenchment became necessary, they retired to nothing more terrifying than soft berths in the Central Committee or in the institutes of the Academy of Sciences.

zh: 因此，第二次改革的对象和改革者的视角都更为柔和。这一次的较量，将发生在斯大林1930年代伟大社会晋升的体弱多病受益者所养育的危机缠身的制度，与“六十年代人”（shestidesiatniki）——他们自己此时也年近六十——之间。至少新改革是这样开始的——直到这场较量发展出自己的势头，远远超出任何在内党封闭的权力圈子里成长起来的群体的愿望。
en: Thus, both the object of reform and the perspective of the reformers were more mellow the second time around. This time the contest would be between the crisis-wracked system nurtured by the valetudinarian beneficiaries of Stalin’s great social promotion of the thirties and the “men of the sixties,” the

, who themselves were now nearing sixty. At least this is the way the new reform started out—until the contest developed a momentum of its own that went far beyond the aspirations of any group raised within the seraglio of the Inner Party.

zh: “加速”
en: “ACCELERATION”

zh: 通向新时代的最初步骤是在旧时代的半影中迈出的。在勃列日涅夫政权停滞的外表背后，人们对制度状况有许多质疑，甚至焦虑。这些关切部分地出现在1982年勃列日涅夫去世到1985年戈尔巴乔夫当选总书记之间两年多的过渡期；在此期间，该职位先后由尤里·安德罗波夫和康斯坦丁·契尔年科占据。虽然表面上延续了勃列日涅夫时代，但鉴于制度的约束，这一时期是不可或缺的，既是为了送走年迈的领导集团，也是为了提供必要的心理冲击，使“重建”终于显得势在必行。
en: The first moves leading to the new era were made in the penumbra of the old. Behind the Brezhnev regime’s facade of immobility there was much questioning, even anxiety, about the state of the system. These concerns partially emerged during the two-year interregnum between Brezhnev’s death in 1982 and Gorbachev’s election as General Secretary in 1985, an interval when that post was successively occupied by Iurii Andropov and Konstantin Chernenko. Although outwardly a continuation of the Brezhnev era, this period was indispensable—given the constraints of the system—both for disposing of the gerontocracy and for providing the psychological shock necessary to make “restructuring” at last appear imperative.

zh: 老卫队的领导人约在1980年前后开始消失：柯西金1979年去世，苏斯洛夫1982年去世，勃列日涅夫本人则在同年几个月后去世。随后，该群体中的次级人物——以契尔年科为代表——与安德罗波夫领导的“改革党”之间展开了继承权竞争。在军方支持下，安德罗波夫迅速从克格勃被提升到中央委员会中苏斯洛夫的职位，以便让他更有条件接替勃列日涅夫。几个月后勃列日涅夫去世，六十八岁的安德罗波夫如期接任。但作为妥协，他的对手契尔年科被留在党的第二职位上，这表明准改革派与老卫队之间的竞争远未结束。
en: The leaders of the old guard began to disappear around 1980: Kosygin died in 1979, Suslov in 1982, and Brezhnev himself a few months later that year. A contest for the succession then developed between the secondary figures of this group, represented by Chernenko, and the “reform party,” led by Andropov. With the support of the military, Andropov was promoted quickly from the KGB to Suslov’s post in the Central Committee in order to position him better to succeed Brezhnev. When Brezhnev died a few months later, Andropov, at age sixty-eight, duly took over. But, in a compromise, his rival, Chernenko, was left in the second Party position, thereby indicating that the contest between would-be reformers and the old guard was far from concluded.

zh: 此时苏联精英中存在一股对安德罗波夫的小范围崇拜，视他为有远见的人，因此把他的短暂统治描述为对抗苏联衰落斗争中的又一次错失机会。但安德罗波夫是斯大林时代的纯粹产物、苏斯洛夫的门生，尽管他了解制度的缺陷，却极不可能有任何非常激进的补救方案；他短暂执政期间的实际表现也证明了这一点。他看到的只是“绩效危机，而不是制度危机”。
因此，他着手研究制度的问题，委托他多年来培养的知识分子顾问撰写机密报告，但他也通过打压半异见者罗伊·梅德韦杰夫——唯一尚未被关押的（多少有些）批评人物——表明了创新的限度。至于其他方面，他只启动了最经典的苏联改革：用警察减少腐败，并加强劳动纪律；这两项政策一如既往，产生了短期成功，却没有触及根本原因。
en: There existed at this time among the Soviet elite a minor cult of Andropov as a man of vision, a view that presented his short reign, therefore, as another lost opportunity in the battle against Soviet decline. But it is most doubtful that Andropov, a pure product of the Stalin era and a protégé of Suslov, for all his awareness of the system’s deficiencies, had in mind any very radical remedies; and this is what his brief empirical record bears out. He saw only a “crisis of performance, not a crisis of the system.”

Thus, he proceeded to study the problems of the system by commissioning confidential reports from advisors among the intelligentsia whom he had cultivated over the years, but he also indicated the limits of innovation by cracking down on the demidissident Roy Medvedev, the sole (somewhat) critical figure still at large. For the rest, he initiated only the most classic type of Soviet reform: He used the police to reduce corruption and to tighten labor discipline, two policies that, as usual, produced short-term success without affecting fundamental causes.

zh: 然而，安德罗波夫有两项举措超越了这些措施。首先，他对学术知识分子的呼吁产生了《新西伯利亚报告》，该报告由社会学家塔季扬娜·扎斯拉夫斯卡娅于1983年撰写，她是阿甘别吉扬在科学院西伯利亚分院的同事。

扎斯拉夫斯卡娅用正统语言提出激进批评，认为苏联中央计划已经过时——实际上是生产的桎梏——而苏联社会远非官方宣传所描绘的和谐统一，而是被统治者与被统治者之间的冲突所撕裂，并因工人阶级的异化、冷漠和缺乏动力而受阻。这一分析指向制度的危机，而不仅仅是其绩效的危机。隐含的补救办法当然是权力下放、激励措施，以及在整个制度中激发个人主动性。这份文件在曾被说成具有致命性的1984年泄露给西方媒体，第一次让世界警觉到苏联稳定的即将终结。它重述了1960年代经济学家的许多诊断，并预示了不久将成为改革的大部分内容。
en: Yet Andropov was responsible for two initiatives that went beyond these measures. First, his appeal to academic intellectuals yielded the
, which was written in 1983 by the sociologist Tatiana Zaslavskaia, a colleague of Aganbegyan in the Siberian branch of the Academy.

Advancing radical criticisms in orthodox language, Zaslavskaia argued that Soviet central planning had become obsolete—indeed a fetter on production—and that Soviet society, far from being the harmonious unity depicted in official propaganda, was riven by conflicts between the rulers and the ruled, and hobbled by alienation, apathy, and lack of motivation among the working class. This analysis pointed to a crisis of the system, not just of its performance. And the implied remedy was, of course, decentralization, incentives, and the stimulation of individual initiative throughout the system. This document, leaked to the Western press in the once putatively fatal year 1984, first alerted the world to the impending end of Soviet stability. zh: 安德罗波夫的第二个重要举措是把米哈伊尔·戈尔巴乔夫当作自己的指定接班人。戈尔巴乔夫于1978年、四十七岁时被调到莫斯科，领导中央委员会书记处的农业部。1981年，主要由于安德罗波夫的推动，他成为政治局最年轻的成员。（然而，安德罗波夫对改革人才的鉴别力并非万无一失，因为他也把盖达尔·阿利耶夫和格里戈里·罗曼诺夫这类顽固的党务官僚提拔到这一级别。）在此期间，戈尔巴乔夫结识了安德罗波夫在其整个生涯中聚集在身边的知识分子，其中大多数人后来成为改革智囊团的一部分。特别是，他参与了产生《新西伯利亚报告》的磋商。戈尔巴乔夫还出国访问，以展示苏联政策的改革面孔。1983年他访问加拿大，在那里第一次见到亚历山大·雅科夫列夫；雅科夫列夫是另一位中央委员会现代化派，当时任驻渥太华大使，因自由主义而处于外交流放的第十个年头。次年，安德罗波夫去世后，作为假定继承人，他进行了一次实际上是国事访问的伦敦之行，首相玛格丽特·撒切尔宣布他是西方“可以与之打交道”的苏联领导人。
en: Andropov’s second important initiative was to treat Mikhail Gorbachev as his designated successor. Gorbachev had been brought to Moscow in 1978, at age forty-seven, to head the Agricultural Department of the Central Committee Secretariat. In 1981, largely at Andropov’s urging, he became the youngest member of the Politburo. (Andropov’s flair for reformist talent, however, was not infallible, for he also promoted to that rank such hidebound apparatchiki as Geidar Aliev and Grigorii Romanov.) During this period Gorbachev became acquainted with the intellectuals whom Andropov had gathered around himself throughout his career, and most of these would later become part of the brain trust of

. And Gorbachev travelled abroad to display the reformist face of Soviet policy. In 1983 he toured Canada, where he first met Aleksandr Yakovlev, another Central Committee modernizer who was then ambassador to Ottawa and in the tenth year of diplomatic exile for his liberalism. The next year, after Andropov’s death, and now as heir presumptive, he made what was virtually a state visit to London, where Prime Minister Margaret Thatcher declared him to be a Soviet leader the West “could do business with.”

zh: 但安德罗波夫死得太早，戈尔巴乔夫未能立即接替他。在又一次妥协中，七十三岁的契尔年科得到职位，戈尔巴乔夫升至第二号位置。次年，1985年，继承问题再次出现时，勃列日涅夫派的候选人是七十二岁的维克托·格里申，莫斯科党组织的相当腐败的头目。但这一次老卫队分裂了。元老安德烈·葛罗米柯和米哈伊尔·索洛缅采夫把力量投向戈尔巴乔夫，克格勃首脑维克托·切布里科夫也是如此；他们还得到一些有影响但不在政治局的中央委员会负责人的支持，如叶戈尔·利加乔夫。再加上把投票安排在格里申的两名支持者赶回莫斯科之前，这使戈尔巴乔夫以一票优势胜出——如果事情确实是由正式投票决定的话。无论如何，即使格里申勉强胜出，领导层的代际更替也不可能长期推迟，因为上层太多人此时感到，不改革已经变得极其危险。
en: But Andropov died too soon for Gorbachev to become his immediate successor. In what was yet another compromise, the seventy-three-year-old Chernenko got the job, and Gorbachev rose to the number two position. The next year, 1985, when the succession opened again, the candidate of the Brezhnevites was the seventy-two-year-old Viktor Grishin, the rather corrupt boss of the Moscow Party. But this time the old guard divided. Elders Andrei Gromyko and Mikhail Solomentsev threw their weight to Gorbachev, as did KGB chief Viktor Chebrikov, and they had the support of influential Central Committee chiefs who were not on the Politburo, such as Yegor Ligachev. This, together with scheduling the ballot before a couple of Grishin supporters could get back to Moscow, put Gorbachev over by one vote, if the matter was indeed settled by a formal vote. In any event, even if Grishin had squeaked in, a generational change of leadership could not have been deferred for long, for too many people at the top now felt that failure to change had become downright dangerous.

zh: 这位新总书记是怎样的人？

人们常常断言，如果苏联制度真正是极权主义的，它就不可能产生如此令人耳目一新的大胆领袖。而他给苏联事务带来的风格上的激进变化，似乎确实活生生地证明制度拥有真正改革的内部资源。然而实际上，戈尔巴乔夫即使在大胆时，也完全是制度的产物——当然比制度中的平均领导人更有才华，但仍然是苏联领导人。至于所谓极权主义无法产生充满活力的人物，制度并非通过把人变成自动机来运作。相反，它的运作方式是为所有领导它的人设定结构性边界和精神视野，而戈尔巴乔夫大体上就在这些参数内活动。的确，他升至最高层不是侥幸，而是现有寡头集团为维护制度而作出的自我保全反应的结果。这样一位精力充沛的人物从勃列日涅夫式停滞中产生，并不比斯大林从列宁的政治局中产生、或赫鲁晓夫从斯大林的主席团中产生更神奇。
en: What manner of man was the new General Secretary?

It has often been alleged that if the Soviet system were really totalitarian it could not have produced so refreshingly bold a leader. And the radical change of style he brought to Soviet affairs did seem to be living proof that the system possessed the inner resources for genuine reform. In fact, however, Gorbachev, even in his boldness, was very much a product of the system—much more talented than its average leader, to be sure, but a Soviet leader nonetheless. As for the supposed incapacity of totalitarianism to bring forth dynamic personalities, it was not by turning individuals into automatons that the system worked. It worked, rather, by setting structural bounds and mental horizons for all those who led it, and Gorbachev operated largely within these parameters. Indeed, his rise to the top was no fluke but the result of a reflex of self-preservation of the system on the part of the existing oligarchy. And it is no more miraculous that such a dynamo came out of Brezhnevite stagnation than that Stalin emerged from Lenin’s Politburo, or Khrushchev from Stalin’s Presidium.

zh: 戈尔巴乔夫通往顶层的道路是苏联党务官僚的经典仕途阶梯，只是更快。他1931年出生在北高加索盛产粮食的斯塔夫罗波尔地区，正值集体化和饥荒之中。他的两个祖父都被去富农化，但他的父亲仍然成为党员、红军战士和优秀的集体农庄庄员。戈尔巴乔夫本人则通过接受中等教育、在机器拖拉机站工作、领导当地共青团组织而在社会上攀升。后一项工作使他在年仅十八岁时成为党的候补党员，随后他获得了进入莫斯科国立大学这一罕见特权。他在那里学习法律，这门学科在当时只对党务和行政生涯有用。
en: Gorbachev’s road to the top was the classic

of the Soviet apparatchik, only faster. He was born in 1931 in the midst of collectivization and famine in the grain-rich region of Stavropol in the North Caucasus. Both of his grandfathers were dekulakized, but his father nonetheless became a Party member, a Red Army soldier, and a good kolkhoznik. Gorbachev himself moved up in the world by receiving a secondary education, working in a Machine Tractor Station, and heading the local Komsomol organization. The latter job made him a candidate member of the Party at the precocious age of eighteen, whereupon he obtained the rare privilege of attending Moscow State University. There he studied law, a discipline that at the time was useful only for a career in Party and administrative affairs.

children: 〔译注〕戈尔巴乔夫两位祖父的受迫害经历并不相同；外祖父戈普卡洛1937年遭政治指控逮捕，不宜笼统称两人都经历了同一种“去富农化”。
〔译注〕戈尔巴乔夫两位祖父的受迫害经历并不相同；外祖父戈普卡洛1937年遭政治指控逮捕，不宜笼统称两人都经历了同一种“去富农化”。

zh: 戈尔巴乔夫在莫斯科大学三年级时，斯大林去世，解冻开始。这一时期他住在斯特罗明卡街的旧宿舍，那里当时是知识探索和质疑制度的场所。还有一丝世界主义色彩：他的一位同学是捷克学生兹德涅克·姆利纳尔，戈尔巴乔夫与他保持联系到1960年代，而此人后来成为1968年《行动纲领》的作者之一。
换句话说，戈尔巴乔夫从二十二岁这个易受影响的年纪起，就与改革共产主义的拥护者密切接触。而在1956年，他甚至成为关键的二十大代表。
en: In Gorbachev’s third year at Moscow State, Stalin died and the thaw began. Gorbachev lived during this period in the old dormitory on Stromynka Street, then a place of intellectual questing and questioning of the system. There was also a touch of cosmopolitanism: one of his classmates was a Czech student, Zdenek Mlynar, with whom Gorbachev kept up contact into the 1960s and who would be one of the authors of the Action Program of 1968.

In other words, Gorbachev was in close contact with proponents of Reform Communism from the impressionable age of twenty-two. And in 1956 he would even be a delegate at the pivotal Twentieth Party Congress.

zh: 但要参加那次大会，他首先必须回到斯塔夫罗波尔，在机关的等级体系中向上攀升。党务生涯的康庄大道是从共青团行政工作开始，戈尔巴乔夫少年时代在家乡省、后来在大学期间就已经从事这项工作。回到斯塔夫罗波尔后，他迅速沿阶梯上升为共青团第一书记，然后成为市第一书记，并于1970年、年仅三十九岁时成为地区第一书记。这种快速晋升的一个原因是他始终有强大的赞助人，特别是费奥多尔·库拉科夫；库拉科夫是前斯塔夫罗波尔第一书记，后来领导中央委员会农业部，并且是政治局委员。在他的庇护下，戈尔巴乔夫还获得了农业创新者的实际经验和全国知名度。此外，斯塔夫罗波尔地区是莫斯科党领导人前来疗养的度假地所在地，地区第一书记当然有义务照顾他们的需要。戈尔巴乔夫就这样结识了整个最高层；他经常见到柯西金，更重要的是见到安德罗波夫和苏斯洛夫，后者本人也是前斯塔夫罗波尔第一书记。因此，1978年库拉科夫去世时，戈尔巴乔夫被任命接替他在中央委员会的职位。次年他成为政治局候补委员，再下一年成为正式委员。这是快进式的完美党务生涯。而在四十九岁时，他是体制内改革派中最年轻的成员，因此按说是最终的领导人。
en: But to get to that Congress, he first had to go back to Stavropol and work his way up the hierarchy of the apparat. The royal road to a Party career was to begin with Komsomol administration, in which Gorbachev had already been engaged in his home province during adolescence and then during his years at the University. Back in Stavropol, he quickly moved up the ladder to First Secretary of the Komsomol, then to First Secretary of the city, and in 1970, at only thirty-nine, to First Secretary of the region. One reason for this rapid advancement was that he always enjoyed powerful sponsors, in particular Fedor Kulakov, the former Stavropol First Secretary who had gone on to head the Agricultural Department of the Central Committee and was a Politburo member. Under his aegis Gorbachev also acquired practical experience and national notoriety as an innovator in agriculture. The Stavropol region, moreover, was home to the resort where Party leaders from Moscow went for a cure, and the regional First Secretary, of course, was obligated to tend to their needs. In this way, Gorbachev met the whole high command; he frequently saw Kosygin and, even more important, Andropov and Suslov, the latter himself a former Stavropol First Secretary. When Kulakov died in 1978, therefore, Gorbachev was appointed to his position on the Central Committee. The next year he became a candidate member of the Politburo, and the following year a full member. It was the perfect Party career in fast forward. And at age forty-nine he was the youngest member, and thus putatively the eventual leader, of the establishment reform party.

zh: 1985年他最终成为领袖时，心里想的是什么改革纲领？由于他显然不能事先宣布全部意图而仍成为领袖，答案在当时并不清楚，甚至现在也不完全清楚。下台后，戈尔巴乔夫开始宣称，改革实际上按照他原先设想的方式发展了——当然，除了苏联解体之外。换句话说，他坚持说，他从一开始的目标就是用“民主”取代“极权主义”，并“解放”东欧。而且东方和西方都有许多观察家把这些成就归功于他。但戈尔巴乔夫后来关于这一主题的所有说法都有理由事先加以怀疑，因为如果属实，那就意味着他曾是反对自己所领导的党和国家的秘密阴谋家。这些说法也不符合我们掌握的有限经验证据。
en: In 1985, when he finally became leader, what program of reform did Gorbachev have in mind? Since he obviously could not announce his full intentions in advance and still become leader, the answer was not clear at the time and is not completely clear even now. After his fall, Gorbachev took to declaring that

had in fact developed the way he had intended it to—with the exception of the Soviet Union’s dissolution, of course. In other words, he maintained that his aims from the beginning had been to replace “totalitarianism” with “democracy” and to “liberate” Eastern Europe. And there are numerous observers, both in the East and in the West, who credit him with these accomplishments. But all of Gorbachev’s later statements on this subject may be doubted a priori, for if true they would mean that he had been a secret conspirator against the Party and the state of which he was in charge. Nor do these statements fit with the limited empirical evidence we possess.

zh: 我们所知道的是，他深切关心制度的未来以及该国继续作为超级大国的地位。他公开表示，如果苏联要以无愧于大国的姿态进入下一个世纪，就需要“激进”措施。
他还觉得，整个苏联生活方式已变得令人窒息、使人衰弱、有损人的尊严。正如他在1990年底透露的，他和另一位高加索改革共产主义者爱德华·谢瓦尔德纳泽在1984年的一次秘密谈话中一致认为，“一切都烂透了”，“不能再这样生活下去了”——这种评价从1970年代末起在苏联精英中并不罕见。但最能揭示他最初意图的，是他在1984年12月发表的一次讲话。
en: What we do know is that he was deeply concerned about the future of the system and about the country’s continued status as a superpower. And he stated publicly that he believed “radical” measures were needed “if the Soviet Union were to enter the next century in a manner worthy of a great power.”

He also felt that the whole Soviet way of life had become stifling, debilitating, and demeaning for the population. As he revealed in late 1990, he and another Caucasian reform Communist, Edvard Shevardnadze, had agreed in a confidential conversation in 1984 that “everything is rotten” and that “it’s no longer possible to live this way”—an evaluation not infrequently heard among the Soviet elite from the late 1970s onward. But the most revealing statement of his initial intentions is a speech he delivered in December 1984.

zh: 戈尔巴乔夫首先承认经济急剧衰退，因而危及苏联的超级大国地位。他宣称补救办法是迅速转向“集约”经济发展、“提高劳动生产率”和“科学技术进步的突破”。这些目标可以通过“使机床工业现代化”（苏联的一句标准口号）以及某种未具体说明的利用“价格、利润、信贷等”经济杠杆来实现，当然还可以通过经济管理的权力下放来实现。但他超越了这种相当标准的利伯曼主义重申，建议“改进苏联政治制度”；其形式可以是工人通过选举产生的苏维埃即委员会“参与”管理，这一提议让人想起捷克斯洛伐克和其他东欧改革。他还呼吁“公开性”、即有关制度弊病的新闻“公开”，因为只有这种“开放”才能抵消“官僚主义扭曲”，并释放人民的创造性智慧。最后，他呼吁实行“法治”，以振兴党并推进“人民的社会主义自我管理”事业。
en: Gorbachev began by recognizing that the economy was in sharp decline and thus imperilling the Soviet Union’s superpower status. He declared that the remedy was a rapid transition to “intensive” economic development, “increased labor productivity,” and a “break-through … of scientific-technical progress.” These objectives could be achieved by “modernizing the machine tool industry” (a standard Soviet shibboleth) and by some unspecified use of such economic levers as “prices, profit, credit, and others,” and, of course, by decentralization of economic management. But he went beyond this fairly standard reassertion of Libermanism to suggest “improvements of the Soviet political system”; these could take the form of “participation” of workers in management by means of elected soviets, or councils, a proposal reminiscent of the Czechoslovak and other East European reforms. And he also called for “

,” or “publicity” of information, about the ills afflicting the system, for only such “openness” could counteract “bureaucratic distortions” and unleash the creative intelligence of the population. Finally, he called for the “rule of law” in order to revivify the Party and advance the cause of “socialist self-government by the people.”

zh: 简言之，这一重建纲领与后来改革的议程相当接近，很大程度上是对苏联集团其他地方响起的熟悉改革主题的重述。沿着这些路线的措施，基本上是“影子异见者”——叶夫图申科所称的“二十大的孩子”——或者他们自称的中央委员会伽利略派的共同财产；这些人正是戈尔巴乔夫在安德罗波夫治下协商准备《新西伯利亚报告》等机密评估时咨询过的人。但这并不意味着他的纲要构成了一项在改革开始时就已经存在的宏大行动计划。讲话只提出了一般目标，对如何实现这些目标只给出极少提示；它在所有问题上的语言都是含糊的，而且对未来转型中的核心问题——权力和党的作用——只字未提。因此，最好把它解读为戈尔巴乔夫思想一个侧面的反映，解读为他的更高希望的标志，而不是具体的改革纲领。这个具体纲领是在总书记应对他所面对的现实时，以务实、即兴的方式出现的。
en: In short, this program of restructuring, which approximates quite closely the future agenda of

, is largely a recapitulation of familiar reformist themes sounded elsewhere in the Soviet bloc. And measures along these lines were pretty much the common property of the “shadow dissidents”—“the children of the Twentieth Party Congress,” as Yevtushenko called them—or of the Galileos of the Central Committee, as they called themselves, the people with whom Gorbachev had consulted under Andropov in the preparation of such confidential assessments as the
. But this does not mean that his outline program constituted a grand design for action that was present at the beginning of

. The speech set forth only general goals, and it gave no more than the sparsest of hints of how these might be achieved; its language on all points was vague, and it said nothing about the central problem—power and the role of the Party—in any future transformation. Thus, it is best read as a reflection of one facet of Gorbachev’s thinking, as an indication of his higher hopes, and not as a concrete program for reform. This concrete program emerged pragmatically, in ad hoc fashion, as the General Secretary grappled with the realities he confronted.

zh: 戈尔巴乔夫开始时在国际事务上大胆行动，在国内事务上则较为谨慎。之所以采取这些对比鲜明的路线，是因为迅速摆脱国际竞争对于处理关键而更棘手的国内经济问题是必要的。然而，这并不意味着漠视、更不意味着放弃苏联的超级大国地位：在整个生涯中，戈尔巴乔夫始终坚持他的国家作为大国的尊严。改革所涉及的，毋宁说是优先次序的改变：复兴的苏联经济是维持超级大国地位不可或缺的前提。
en: Gorbachev began with a mixture of boldness in international affairs and prudence in domestic ones. The reason for these contrasting courses was that prompt liberation from international competition was necessary to address the crucial, and more intractable, internal problems of the economy. However, this did not mean indifference to, still less abandonment of, the Soviet Union’s superpower status: throughout his career, Gorbachev always insisted on his country’s dignity as a great state. What was involved in
, rather, was a change of priorities: a revived Soviet economy was the indispensable precondition for maintaining superpower status.

zh: 因此，苏联需要从国际竞争中取得一个“喘息空间”，以便在国内恢复元气，然后重返与资本主义的较量。因为如果认为戈尔巴乔夫已不再以社会主义的最终优越性、因而以两个阵营之间的意识形态对立为思考框架，那就错了。然而在他看来，它们之间的竞争此时必须采取比最近过去更温和、更少危险的形式；而社会主义必须使自己的结构现代化并大大提高绩效，才能实现其真正潜力。尽管戈尔巴乔夫后来逐渐不得不抛弃这些竞争力幻想——他永远不会放弃社会主义观念本身——但在开始时，他寻求的是完善苏联遗产，而不是超越它。
en: Thus the Soviet Union needed a “breathing space” from international competition in order to recoup internally before returning to the contest with capitalism. For it would be a mistake to think that Gorbachev had ceased thinking in terms of the ultimate superiority of socialism, and thus of the ideological polarity between the two camps. The competition between them, however, in his view now had to assume more muted and less dangerous forms than it had taken in the recent past; and socialism had to modernize its structures and improve its performance greatly if it were to realize its true potential. Although Gorbachev would gradually be obliged to shed these illusions of competitiveness—he would never abandon the socialist idea itself—at the beginning he sought to perfect the Soviet heritage, not to transcend it.

zh: 因此，他的第一个举动是一种布列斯特—立陶夫斯克式的行动，其形式是几乎单方面退出冷战，以便把所有精力转向国内改革，因为戈尔巴乔夫认真对待他的列宁主义。

他经常表示钦佩奠基人的大胆，并在担任总书记之初推崇米哈伊尔·沙特罗夫赞美列宁年代的戏剧。正如列宁在布列斯特—立陶夫斯克挽救了处于第一次生存危机中的苏维埃国家，戈尔巴乔夫现在也要通过类似的大胆表现，在新危机中挽救它。此外，像所有总书记一样，他必须成为“他那个时代的列宁”：苏联万神殿中已没有其他神祇，也没有其他充满活力和胆识的象征可以用来推动这个迟钝的制度。而戈尔巴乔夫像任何处于权力顶峰的人一样有野心，而且正如事件将表明的，还颇为虚荣。
en: His first move, therefore, was a kind of Brest-Litovsk that took the form of a nearly unilateral withdrawal from the Cold War in order to turn all energies to reform on the home front, for Gorbachev took his Leninism seriously.

He frequently asserted his admiration for the Founder’s audacity, and at the beginning of his general secretaryship he promoted Mikhail Shatrov’s plays extolling the Lenin years. Just as Lenin at Brest-Litovsk had saved the Soviet state in its first crisis of survival, Gorbachev would now save it in a new crisis by a similar display of audacity. Moreover, like all General Secretaries, he had to be the “Lenin of his day”: There was no other deity left in the Soviet pantheon, and no other symbol of dynamism and daring with which to move the sluggish system. And Gorbachev, like anyone else at the pinnacle of power, was ambitious and, as events would show, not a little vain.

zh: 他回到布列斯特-立陶夫斯克，首先意味着放弃SS-20，从而退出与美国的核竞争；其次意味着退出一切第三世界冒险，从阿富汗开始。

这种收缩不仅是内部改革的必要前奏，而且外交政策是总书记作为苏联行政首脑最容易主动制定政策的领域。因此，他几乎第一个正式行动就是表示渴望与里根总统举行峰会，并宣布单方面暂停部署SS-20七个月。自1979年《第二阶段限制战略武器条约》签署以来，苏美一直没有举行峰会，在此期间发生了所谓的第二次冷战：入侵阿富汗、1981年镇压团结工会（这促使莫斯科恢复对西方电台的干扰，这一做法在1982年后被放弃）、1983年击落大韩航空007号班机，以及同年中止核军备谈判。此外，里根在第一任期内已成为苏联人眼中具有神话般侵略性的人物。在缓和的抚慰做法之后，莫斯科面对的是前所未有的美国军事建设，其顶点是1983年的战略防御计划（SDI），并伴随着关于“邪恶帝国”的令人警觉的言论。可以公正地说，在安德罗波夫治下，苏联领导层中许多人相信美国实际上在寻求战争，这种信念强化了所有关于帝国主义的旧学说。
因此，为降低温度，契尔年科缓和了关于美国“希特勒”的叫嚣，并恢复了军备谈判。
en: His return to Brest-Litovsk meant, first, withdrawing from nuclear competition with the United States by giving up the SS-20s, and, second, withdrawing from all Third World adventures, beginning with Afghanistan.

Not only was such retrenchment a necessary preliminary to internal reform, but foreign policy was the area where the General Secretary, as the Soviet executive, could most easily initiate policy. Accordingly, almost his first official act was to indicate his eagerness for a summit with President Reagan and to announce a unilateral seven-month moratorium on deployment of the SS-20s. There had been no Soviet-American summit since the signing of SALT II in 1979, and in the interim the so-called second Cold War had taken place: the Afghan invasion, the suppression of Solidarity in 1981 (which occasioned resumed jamming of Western radio by Moscow, a practice abandoned after 1982), the shooting down of KAL 007 in 1983, and the suspension of nuclear arms negotiations the same year. Moreover, Reagan in his first term had become a figure of mythic aggressiveness to the Soviets. After the soothing practices of détente, Moscow was confronted with an unprecedented American military buildup that culminated in the Strategic Defense Initiative (SDI) of 1983 and was accompanied by alarming rhetoric about the “Evil Empire.” It is fair to say that under Andropov many in the Soviet leadership believed the United States actually sought war, a belief that reinforced all of the old doctrines about imperialism.
To lower the temperature, therefore, Chernenko had toned down vociferation about the American “Hitler” and had resumed arms negotiations.

zh: 但认真应对超级大国竞争的深层问题，仍要由戈尔巴乔夫来完成。对苏联人来说，第一个问题是他们衰退的经济，这使他们不可能匹配美国的国防建设，尤其是SDI的技术飞跃。后者是否会给美国提供对付苏联弹道导弹的实际防御，并不是核心问题。更重要的是地缘政治要点：SDI提出了一个苏联既不能忽视也不能匹敌的技术和经济挑战。因此，化解这一挑战的唯一途径是谈判，于是戈尔巴乔夫把结束冷战作为他的第一优先。西方许多人无疑会质疑这种关于转向结束冲突的说法，但前苏联军事人员和政策分析家普遍同意，苏联无力维持其在军备竞赛中的那一半，特别是在SDI方面，是触发改革的主要因素。这一结论因1984年尼古拉·奥加尔科夫元帅有点神秘的解职而得到加强；奥加尔科夫是契尔年科治下的苏联国防部长，看来他主张苏联技术的相对衰落威胁国家的超级大国地位，因此军方应在经济政策中获得更大发言权。
奥加尔科夫因此指出了现局势的地缘政治危险，却提出了一个危及党至高无上地位的对策，于是招致对军方本身的拒绝。
en: But it remained for Gorbachev to grapple seriously with the underlying problems of superpower competition. For the Soviets, the first of these was their declining economy, which left them with no possibility of matching the American defense buildup, and in particular the technological leap of SDI. Whether the latter would have provided the United States with a practical defense against Soviet ballistic missiles is not the central question. More important is the geopolitical point that SDI posed a technological and economic challenge the Soviets could neither ignore nor match. Hence, the only way to defuse the challenge was through negotiation, and so Gorbachev made winding down the Cold War his first priority. Many in the West would undoubtedly dispute this version of the turn towards ending that conflict, but former Soviet military personnel and political analysts generally agree that the Soviet Union’s inability to keep up its half of the arms race, in particular with regard to SDI, was a principal factor in triggering

. This conclusion is reinforced by the somewhat enigmatic firing in 1984 of Marshal Nikolai Ogarkov, the Soviet minister of defense under Chernenko, who it seems was arguing that the comparative decline of Soviet technology threatened the country’s superpower status, and that the military, therefore, should receive a greater say in economic policy.
Ogarkov thus identified the geopolitical danger of the existing situation but advanced a remedy that menaced Party supremacy, and so provoked a rebuff to the military as such.

zh: 戈尔巴乔夫进一步降低了军方的角色，没有让新任国防部长谢尔盖·索科洛夫元帅成为政治局正式委员；二十年来军方第一次在那个机构中没有席位。与此同时，1985年7月，戈尔巴乔夫解除葛罗米柯的外交部长职务，任命谢瓦尔德纳泽接替他，后者也成为政治局正式委员。由于谢瓦尔德纳泽除了与总书记个人关系密切之外没有资格担任此职，这也清楚表明戈尔巴乔夫亲自掌管对外关系，并把缓和作为其政策的基石。
en: Gorbachev reduced the role of the military still further by not naming the new minister of defense, Marshal Sergei Sokolov, a full member of the Politburo; for the first time in two decades the military was without a seat on that body. At the same time, in July 1985, Gorbachev removed Gromyko as foreign minister and appointed in his place Shevardnadze, who also became a full Politburo member. Since Shevardnadze had no qualifications for the job other than his personal closeness to the General Secretary, this also was a clear signal that Gorbachev was personally taking charge of foreign relations and would make détente the cornerstone of his policy.

zh: 但要使这场赌博成功，戈尔巴乔夫需要一个他能够与之打交道的美国总统，而事实证明，第二任期的里根准备做一笔交易。正如一位专家所说：“里根是个简单直率的人，他字面理解‘从实力地位谈判’的原则：一旦建立了实力，就进行谈判。”
事实证明，里根也有几分赌徒气质，愿意与莫斯科的新人冒险；他甚至有富于远见的一面，不仅表现在SDI这样的计划上，也表现在他愿意与苏联分享该计划并废除所有核武器上。因此，戈尔巴乔夫很快就能够展示他冒险向华盛顿示好的成果，从而使国内正统派批评者失去攻击的把柄。
en: But for this gamble to work, Gorbachev needed an American president

could do business with, and it turned out that the Reagan of the second term was ready to make a deal. As one specialist put it: “A simple and straightforward man, Reagan took the principle of ‘negotiation from strength’ literally: once one had built strength, one negotiated.”

As it turned out, Reagan, too, was something of a gambler and was willing to take a chance with the new man in Moscow; he even had a visionary side, as expressed not only in a scheme such as SDI but also in his willingness to share that program with the Soviet Union and to do away with all nuclear weapons. So Gorbachev was soon able to show results from his risky overture to Washington, and thus to disarm his orthodox critics at home.

zh: 第一次峰会在1985年底于日内瓦举行。尽管没有产生具体结果，它确实创造了谈判的新气氛，并促成了两位领导人互访的承诺。但戈尔巴乔夫很着急。于是，1986年10月，在没有认真与军方或政治局协商的情况下，他要求在冰岛雷克雅未克的中立地点举行一次临时小型峰会。一到那里，他就提出了此前闻所未闻的前景：消除所有核武器和弹道导弹，而他发现一位美国总统对这个目标持接受态度。戈尔巴乔夫还接受了里根长期提出的在欧洲消除所有中程导弹的“零点方案”。但这一接受附有条件，最重要的一条是SDI研究将限于实验室，其任何组成部分都不会在太空测试。里根不愿接受这一点，于是这场最奇异的峰会无果而终。尽管如此，双方都戏剧性地确认了一个原则：未来的军备协议不能像过去那些大体上装点门面的协议，而必须产生全面削减，否则就根本不值得。正是在这种精神下，长达二十五年的军备控制谈判进程在接下来的三年里完成。
en: The first summit took place in Geneva at the end of 1985. Although it led to no concrete results, it did create a new mood for negotiations and produced a promise of mutual visits by the two leaders. But Gorbachev was in a hurry. So in October 1986, without seriously consulting with the military or the Politburo, he requested an interim minisummit on neutral ground in Reykjavik, Iceland. Once there he raised the hitherto unheard-of prospect of eliminating all nuclear weapons and ballistic missiles, and he found an American president who was receptive to this goal. Gorbachev also accepted Reagan’s long-standing “zero option” proposal for eliminating all intermediate-range missiles in Europe. But there were conditions attached to this acceptance, the most important one being that SDI research would be confined to laboratories and none of its components would be tested in space. This Reagan would not accept, so this most bizarre of summits ended without an agreement. Still, a principle had been dramatically asserted by both sides: Future arms agreements could not be like the largely cosmetic accords of the past, but would have to produce sweeping reductions if they were to be worthwhile at all. And it was in this spirit that the twenty-five-years-long process of arms control negotiations was concluded in the next three years.

〔译注〕双方在雷克雅未克之前已讨论全面消除核武器，苏方1986年1月提出过分阶段方案。此后军控谈判并未在1989年前后结束，第一阶段削减战略武器条约于1991年签订。

zh: 关键的转折点是1987年的《中程核力量条约》。该条约禁止在欧洲直到乌拉尔山的所有中程导弹，基本上认可了里根1981年首次提出的零点方案。换句话说，戈尔巴乔夫本质上是按照西方的条件退出冷战，而且没有在SDI上获得任何让步。毫无疑问，他这样做的原因之一是，到1987年（稍后将解释），改革的内部困难已变得尖锐。而他能够这样做，是因为军方已日益失去信誉。不仅苏联军队正在输掉阿富汗战争，而且1987年5月，一名西德少年驾驶单引擎塞斯纳飞机穿过苏联所有西部雷达，降落在红场！戈尔巴乔夫利用这一惨败解除了军方最高指挥层，并任命自己的人、无足轻重的德米特里·亚佐夫将军为国防部长。
en: The crucial turning point was the INF Treaty of 1987. By banning all intermediate-range missiles in Europe up to the Urals, the treaty basically endorsed the zero option Reagan had first put forward in 1981. In other words, Gorbachev bowed out of the Cold War essentially on the West’s terms, and without obtaining any concessions on SDI. No doubt one reason he did so was that by 1987 (as will be explained shortly) the internal difficulties of

had become acute. And he could get away with doing so because the military had become increasingly discredited. Not only were Soviet forces losing the Afghan war, but in May 1987 a West German teenager piloted a single-engine Cessna airplane through all of the Soviets’ western radar and landed on Red Square! Gorbachev took advantage of this fiasco to fire the military high command and appoint his own man, the insignificant General Dmitrii Yazov, as defense minister.

〔译注〕1987年《中导条约》要求美苏销毁全球范围内射程500至5500公里的陆基弹道和巡航导弹及相关装备，并非只禁止欧洲境内所有种类的中程导弹。

zh: 除了这些同意从欧洲排除中程导弹的具体形势所带来的理由之外，戈尔巴乔夫还受常识推动，对苏联的世界事务观作出根本修正。迄今为止，这种观点认为核军备对马克思列宁主义学说没有任何影响，即国际关系是阶级战争的一种形式；因此核战争既是可设想的，也是可打赢的。赫鲁晓夫用他的“和平共处”淡化了这一点，但他没有放弃必然冲突导致社会主义胜利的学说。戈尔巴乔夫最终得出符合实际的结论：核战争既不可设想，也不可打赢；这一立场正是他在国际事务中“新思维”的精髓。
en: Over and above these circumstantial reasons for agreeing to exclude intermediate-range missiles from Europe, Gorbachev was moved by common sense to make a fundamental revision in the Soviet view of world affairs. Hitherto, this view had been that nuclear armaments made no difference to the Marxist-Leninist doctrine that international relations were a form of class war; nuclear war therefore was both thinkable and winnable. Khrushchev toned this down with his “peaceful coexistence,” but he did not abandon the doctrine of inevitable conflict leading to socialist victory. Gorbachev at last drew the realistic conclusion that nuclear war was neither thinkable nor winnable, a position that was the essence of his “new thinking” in international affairs.

zh: 但这一立场必然要求放弃马克思主义关于阶级斗争的核心原则，无论在国际事务还是在一切人类事务中。戈尔巴乔夫1987年底访问华盛顿签署《中程核力量条约》时，以行动体现了这一立场。1988年12月，他在联合国用语言做到了这一点，宣布他的政府致力于“全人类价值”（马克思曾把这种思想斥为“普遍兄弟情谊的骗局”）。然而，通过含蓄地放弃阶级斗争的优先地位，戈尔巴乔夫无意中削弱了政权的意识形态专政基础；这一后果后来又被他把苏联带入“共同欧洲家园”的言论所强化。这些放弃很快将在苏联这个旧家园中引发冲击波，但在此期间，它们使戈尔巴乔夫成为国际英雄和崇拜对象。而这些放弃确实是他最伟大的历史成就。
en: But this position necessitated abandoning the central Marxist principle of class struggle, in international and in all human affairs. This Gorbachev did in deed when he visited Washington at the end of 1987 for the signing of the INF Treaty. And this he did in words before the United Nations in December of 1988, when he declared his government’s commitment to “universal human values” (Marx had castigated such thinking as the “universal brotherhood swindle”). Yet by implictly renouncing the primacy of class struggle, Gorbachev inadvertently undermined the ideocratic foundations of the regime, a consequence later reinforced by his talk of bringing the Soviet Union into a “common European home.” These renunciations would soon send shock waves through the old Soviet home, but in the meantime they made Gorbachev an international hero and cult figure. And these renunciations were indeed his greatest historical accomplishment.

zh: 1988年，戈尔巴乔夫宣布从阿富汗撤出苏联军队，并承诺在1989年2月前完成；这种放弃同样混合着国家弱点和新确立的原则。苏联第一次放弃了一块曾为社会主义赢得的领土。同样在1988年，戈尔巴乔夫和谢瓦尔德纳泽开始逐步结束苏联和古巴在安哥拉和埃塞俄比亚的介入。次年，他们开始削减对尼加拉瓜桑地诺主义者的援助，甚至对卡斯特罗的古巴的援助。1989年2月，最后一批苏联军队完全按承诺撤离阿富汗。与此同时，苏联的附庸越南被说服撤出柬埔寨。因此到1990年，勃列日涅夫时代的所有苏联承诺都已清理完毕。然而到那时，新布列斯特—立陶夫斯克那种经过计算和“校准”的收缩，早已变成一场溃败。
en: Renunciation continued in a similar mixture of national weakness and new-found principle when, in 1988, Gorbachev announced the withdrawal of Soviet troops from Afghanistan and promised its completion by February 1989. For the first time, the Soviet Union was giving up territory that had once been won for socialism. Also in 1988, Gorbachev and Shevardnadze began liquidating the Soviet and Cuban commitments in Angola and Ethiopia. The following year, they started cutting back aid to the Nicaraguan Sandinistas, and even to Castro’s Cuba. In February 1989, the last Soviet troops left Afghanistan exactly as promised. At the same time, the Soviets’ client, Vietnam, was persuaded to withdraw from Cambodia. Thus by 1990 all of the Soviet commitments of the Brezhnev era had been liquidated. Yet by that date the calculated and “calibrated” retrenchment of the new Brest-Litovsk had long since become a rout.

zh: 的确，在这一进程结束时，除了直接相关的第三世界国家之外，没有多少人对细节感兴趣，因为在1986—1987年最初的国际突破之后，改革这场戏主要在国内舞台上演。事实上，苏联民众一直最关心改革将如何影响他们的日常生活。结束冷战主要是西方的关切，这就是为什么戈尔巴乔夫的国外支持者视他为巨人。然而，他的国内支持者主要关心他如何利用国内的喘息空间，而在这方面，他的地位始终较为有限。
en: Indeed, at the end of this process no one other than the Third World countries directly concerned was much interested in the details, for after the initial international breakthrough of 1986-1987 the drama of
was played out largely on the domestic front. In fact, the Soviet population had always been most interested in how

would affect their daily lives. Ending the Cold War had been primarily a Western preoccupation, and this is why Gorbachev’s external constituency viewed him as a giant. His internal constituency, however, was preoccupied chiefly with the use he made of his breathing space at home, and here his status was always more modest.

zh: 国内的首要任务当然是经济复兴。但鉴于苏联制度无所不包的性质，复兴经济将需要苏联生活的全面重建。戈尔巴乔夫在1985年4月上任后的第一次中央委员会全会上开始谈到这样的新起点，此后数年，苏联官员把生活分为四月前和四月后两个时期。
en: The great internal priority was of course economic revival. But given the all-encompassing nature of the Soviet system, reviving the economy would require a general restructuring of Soviet life. Gorbachev began speaking of such a new departure at his first Central Committee plenum in April 1985, and for several years thereafter Soviet officials spoke of life as being divided into pre- and post-April periods.

zh: 改革一词本身在四月后不久出现，起初主要用来指经济事务。但到次年，按照苏联结构的逻辑，它获得了刚才提到的更广泛含义；到1987年，它与外交政策中的“新思维”一起，已成为新时代的真正咒语，先是指所有制度的“激进”变革，然后指“革命性”变革，甚至指人们内心世界的变革。
en: The term

itself appeared shortly after April, and at first it was used largely to refer to economic matters. But by the next year, in response to the logic of the Soviet structures, it had acquired the broader connotation just mentioned; and by 1987, along with “new thinking” in foreign policy, it had become a veritable mantra of the new era, designating first a “radical,” then a “revolutionary,” transformation of all institutions, indeed of peoples’ inner beings.

zh: 由于改革有多种模糊含义，很难知道戈尔巴乔夫究竟想要什么结果，甚至很难知道他在任何特定时刻的实际政策是什么。事实上，除了实现一种现代化但仍属列宁主义的社会主义之外，他的实际政策很大程度上是即兴制定的，因为事件和制度的抵抗迫使他从一个问题转向另一个问题。改革的实际进程因此相当混乱，甚至矛盾。
en: Because

had multiple and vague meanings, it is difficult to know just what results Gorbachev intended, or even what his operative policy was at any given moment. In fact, other than achieving a modernized but still Leninist socialism, he was largely improvising his operative policy as events and the resistance of the system obliged him to move from one problem to another. The result was a considerable degree of confusion, even contradiction, in the record of

zh: 在经济这一核心领域，戈尔巴乔夫到1988年最终显露的基本目标，是通常改革共产主义纲领的一种变体：通过权力下放软化计划，提供物质激励以鼓励工厂和个人主动性，并引入近似真实的价格。

除此之外，他还增加了在服务业中创建一个小型私营或“合作社”部门的目标。简言之，戈尔巴乔夫的经济纲领明显比柯西金的大胆，甚至比1968年捷克纲领更有雄心，但它几乎没有打破传统共产主义“国家主义”的模子。恰如其分，改革经济雄心的象征变成了列宁的新经济政策，戈尔巴乔夫及其顾问经常援引这一先例来为自己的事业提供合法性。当然，他们不可能真正回到新经济政策，因为已经不存在只需开放农产品市场便能被说服增加生产的独立农民阶层。但新经济政策可以被唤起来，作为一种比斯大林秩序更自由的替代方案的精神，而斯大林秩序在1985年基本上仍然原封未动。
en: In the core area of economics Gorbachev’s basic goals, as they emerged at last by 1988, were a variation on the usual program of Reform Communism: softening the Plan through decentralization, providing material incentives to encourage plant and individual initiative, and introducing an approximation of real prices.

To this he added the aim of creating a small private, or “cooperative,” sector in services. In short, Gorbachev’s economic program was distinctly bolder than Kosygin’s, and even more ambitious than the Czech program of 1968, but it hardly broke the mold of traditional Communist “statism.” Appropriately, the symbol of

’s economic ambition became Lenin’s NEP, and Gorbachev and his advisors often referred to this precedent to legitimize their own enterprise. Of course, they could not really return to the NEP, for there no longer existed an independent peasantry that could be persuaded to produce abundance simply by instituting a free market for their products. But the NEP could be evoked as the spirit of a more liberal alternative to the Stalinist order that in 1985 still remained essentially intact.

zh: 尽管如此，像一些观察家那样把戈尔巴乔夫纲领视为“市场社会主义”将是一个错误。首先，不清楚市场社会主义会是什么样子，因为历史上从未有过真正存在的市场社会主义的案例：这种制度从来只是一种观念和愿望，有点像难以捉摸的“第三条道路”。更重要的是，在改革下，从未考虑建立真正的市场，甚至连新经济政策下存在的那种有限市场也没有。戈尔巴乔夫更不曾考虑放弃“社会主义财产”，无论在工业还是农业中。工业仍将国有化，大多数零售商业也将如此；对集体化农民，所考虑的不过是长期租赁和“联系”制度的各种变体。总之，戈尔巴乔夫的经济纲领虽然在苏联语境中激进，却几乎不是革命性的；如果革命要从改革中产生，它必须作为经济改革的政治副作用出现。
en: Still, it would be a mistake to view Gorbachev’s program as “market socialism,” as some observers have. First, it is not clear what a market socialism would look like, for there has never been a case of a really existing market socialism in history: such a system has never been more than an idea and an aspiration, somewhat like the elusive “third way.” Even more important, under

there was never any question of creating a real market, not even to the limited extent of the market that existed under the NEP. Still less did Gorbachev contemplate giving up “socialist property,” whether in industry or in agriculture. Industry would remain nationalized, as would most retail commerce; and nothing more than long-term leases and variations on the “link” system were ever contemplated for the collectivized peasantry. In sum, Gorbachev’s economic program, though radical in the Soviet context, was hardly revolutionary; if revolution were to emerge from
, it would have to come as a result of the political side effects of the economic reform.

zh: 戈尔巴乔夫相对温和的经济改革，还因引入方式的渐进和谨慎，以及因实施与其相矛盾的传统措施而进一步受到限制。早期，戈尔巴乔夫那些“现代化”经济顾问——如从新西伯利亚半流放中归来的阿甘别吉扬和列昂尼德·阿巴尔金——开始制定措施来实施刚才概述的长期纲领。由于这些措施要到1987年或1988年才准备好，戈尔巴乔夫决定在此期间把经济提升到能够从预期自由化中获益的水平。这一决定产生了改革的第一阶段——加速（uskorenie），即工业进程的“加速”——实际上延续了安德罗波夫的纲领。但这种加速尝试导致采用传统指令措施，实际上使情况更糟。
en: Gorbachev’s relatively moderate economic reform was tempered even more by the gradual and prudent way in which it was introduced, as well as by the application of more-traditional measures that actually contradicted it. Early on, Gorbachev’s “modernizing” economic advisors—such as Aganbegyan, now returned from semiexile in Novosibirsk, and Leonid Abalkin—began working up measures to implement the long-term program just outlined. Since these measures would not be ready until 1987 or 1988, Gorbachev decided to hoist the economy in the meantime to a level where it could profit from the intended liberalization. This decision produced the first phase

, or an “acceleration” of the industrial process—which in effect continued Andropov’s program. But this attempt at acceleration led to the application of traditional command measures that in fact made the situation worse.

zh: 具体而言，加速意味着1985年启动的一项雄心勃勃、代价高昂的机床生产和工业设备更新计划，仿佛这样的计划本身就构成一场“科学技术革命”。与此同时，建立了“国家验收”（gospriemka）质量控制系统：国家检验员有权在商品下线时接受或拒收，以促使管理层和工人更有效率地工作——这是一项让人想起安德罗波夫的纪律措施。同样传统的是戈尔巴乔夫反对“不劳而获收入”的运动——即反对经济运转所必需、而即将建立的合作社本应使之正规化的全部影子活动。在据说是戈尔巴乔夫专长的农业领域，若干部被合并成一个庞大的组织——国家农工委员会（Gosagroprom）——这是完全适得其反的集中化。最后，显然在叶戈尔·利加乔夫的敦促下，戈尔巴乔夫发起了一场反酗酒运动，减少销售点、缩短营业时间，并砍掉南方的葡萄园，从而毁掉了一个有利可图的产业。这场运动的主要结果是私酿酒产量大增（使糖变得如此稀缺，不得不实行配给），国家收入相应急剧下降。的确，这种收入损失，加上工业设备更新计划的成本，加剧了预算赤字，几年内将达到危机程度。因此到1986年底，尽管强制的加速方法产生了轻微的增长冲刺，
却没有做任何事情来重组经济。与此同时，改革的新问题以机关抵抗的形式出现了。
en: Concretely, acceleration meant an ambitious and costly program of machine-tool production and industrial reequipment that was launched in 1985 as if such a program in itself constituted a “scientific-technical revolution.” At the same time, a system of “

,” or quality control, was instituted: state inspectors were empowered to accept or reject goods as they came off the assembly line in order to goad both management and workers into working more efficiently—a disciplinary measure reminiscent of Andropov. In the same tradition was Gorbachev’s campaign against “unearned income”—that is, against all of the shadow activity that was necessary to the functioning of the economy and that the forthcoming creation of cooperatives was supposed to regularize. In agriculture, allegedly Gorbachev’s specialty, a number of ministries were regrouped into a single giant organization, Gosagroprom—a completely counterproductive centralization. Finally, Gorbachev, apparently at the urging of Yegor Ligachev, launched an anti-alcohol drive that cut the number of outlets, shortened their hours, and tore up vineyards in the south, thereby ruining a profitable industry. The principal results of this campaign were a great increase in the private production of moonshine (which made sugar so scarce it had to be rationed) and a correspondingly drastic drop in state revenues. Indeed, this loss of income, together with the costs of the industrial reequipment program, aggravated a budget deficit that in a few years would reach crisis proportions. So by the end of 1986, although the forced methods of acceleration had produced a slight spurt of growth,
nothing had been done to restructure the economy. And in the meantime a new problem for
had emerged in the form of resistance from the apparat.

zh: 当选后，戈尔巴乔夫立即背离了勃列日涅夫的“干部稳定”政策。他恢复其更早前任的积极行动，以招募适合他预期新政策的人员，并首先着眼于更换高层人员。格里申和罗曼诺夫等对手，以及葛罗米柯等过去的留任者，被从政治局撤换，由安德罗波夫的人取代：利加乔夫，书记处的意识形态和人事负责人；尼古拉·雷日科夫，一位工程师和工业管理者，他也成为总理；维克托·切布里科夫，克格勃首脑；以及其他背景相似、倾向温和改革的人。但这些不是戈尔巴乔夫的人——他们是靠自己爬到顶层的，是盟友，不是党徒。除谢瓦尔德纳泽外，戈尔巴乔夫唯一真正的意识形态支持者是雅科夫列夫；他1983年从加拿大被召回，领导社会科学和国际事务智库IMEMO（世界经济和国际关系研究所），然后于1985年被调到书记处宣传部，最后于1987年6月被增补进政治局。而在前一年6月的全会上，鲍里斯·叶利钦成为政治局候补委员；他最近取代格里申担任莫斯科党委第一书记，以清除这个重要领地中的腐败。但这很难说是一个同质的臣属群体，甚至很难说是志同道合的改革者；戈尔巴乔夫从未拥有一个团结在改革背后的最高指挥部，至少就他为自己定义的那个词而言。
en: Immediately after his election, Gorbachev departed from Brezhnev’s policy of “stability of cadres.” He reverted to the activism of his more remote predecessors in order to recruit personnel suited to his intended new policies, and he focused first on replacing people at the top. Rivals such as Grishin and Romanov, and holdovers from the past such as Gromyko, were removed from the Politburo and replaced by Andropov men: Ligachev, the Secretariat’s chief of ideology and chief of personnel; Nikolai Ryzhkov, an engineer and industrial manager, who also became prime minister; Viktor Chebrikov, head of the KGB; and others of similar background and moderately reformist inclination. But these were not Gorbachev men—they had made it to the top on their own, and were allies, not partisans. In addition to Shevardnadze, Gorbachev’s only other real ideological supporter was Yakovlev; he was brought back from Canada in 1983 to head the social-science and international affairs think tank IMEMO (Institute of the World Economy and International Relations), then was moved to the Secretariat’s propaganda department in 1985, and was finally added to the Politburo in June 1987. And at the June plenum of the previous year, Boris Yeltsin, who had recently replaced Grishin as Moscow Party boss in order to clean out the corruption in that major fief, became a candidate member of the Politburo. But this was hardly a homogeneous group of liege men, or even of like-minded reformers; and Gorbachev would never have a high command united behind
at least insofar as he had defined that term for himself.

children: 〔译注〕葛罗米柯1985年卸任外长后仍留在政治局，1988年才退出；叶利钦1986年2月成为政治局候补委员，而非同年6月。
〔译注〕葛罗米柯1985年卸任外长后仍留在政治局，1988年才退出；叶利钦1986年2月成为政治局候补委员，而非同年6月。

zh: 对总书记来说，整个党内的情形更糟。作为积极行动的领导人，戈尔巴乔夫立即行使了任命全国各省和地方第一书记的特权，到1986年中期，他已更换了其中三分之一。

但由于实际任命工作很多是由利加乔夫——书记处人事负责人、因而也是等级体系中的第二号人物——做的，新人结果是更年轻但仍非常正统的党务官僚。戈尔巴乔夫还试图在1986年2月他作为总书记主持的第一次代表大会上震动党。赫鲁晓夫如今令人尴尬的1961年纲领被一份新文件取代，新文件对向完整共产主义过渡只字未提，只承诺到2000年提高生活水平。为实现这一新目标，戈尔巴乔夫第一次呼吁“激进经济改革”，但除了号召促进“加速”之外，他没有说明如何实现这一改革。在重组党方面，戈尔巴乔夫获得了一个新的中央委员会，其中43%的成员是第一次当选。这一变化，连同地区书记的更换，代表了四分之一世纪以来党内人员最大的更替。但随后什么也没有发生：机关照旧缓慢前行，只是口头敷衍经济改革的理念。
en: Matters were even worse for the General Secretary within the Party as a whole. An activist leader, Gorbachev had immediately exercised his prerogative of naming provincial and local First Secretaries throughout the country, and by mid-1986 he had replaced one third of them.

But because it was Ligachev, the Secretariat’s chief of personnel and thus the number two man in the hierarchy, who did much of the actual appointing, the new men turned out to be younger though still very orthodox apparatchiki. Gorbachev also tried to shake up the Party at the first Congress he presided over as General Secretary in February 1986. Khrushchev’s now embarrassing Program of 1961 was replaced by a new document that said nothing about the transition to full Communism but promised only an improved standard of living by the year 2000. To attain this new goal, Gorbachev for the first time called for “radical economic reform,” but beyond exhortations to promote “acceleration” he gave no idea of how this reform was to be achieved. In regard to restructuring the Party, Gorbachev obtained a new Central Committee, 43 percent of whose members were elected for the first time. This change, together with the replacement of regional secretaries, represented the greatest turnover in Party personnel in a quarter century. But then nothing happened: the apparat plodded on as before, paying only lip service to the idea of economic reform.

zh: 公开性
en: GLASNOST

zh: 政治攻势受挫后，戈尔巴乔夫于1986年着手改革的第二项组成政策——公开性。

这个词通常译为“开放”或“公开”，实际上是一个可追溯到亚历山大二世的官僚术语，意味着官方鼓励对政府希望以批判但建设性方式讨论的事情进行公开议论。戈尔巴乔夫在掌权前就渴望开放制度；他现在把它列为优先事项，以批评的刺痛来刺激迟钝的党。但这一政策很快被形势推到意想不到的程度，第一个形势是1986年4月的切尔诺贝利灾难。这场灾难不仅揭示苏联工业状况远比政府所估计的糟糕，而且揭示官方的保密政策使这些灾难性状况以及围绕它们的犯罪性疏忽得以长期存在、甚至加剧。在最初试图掩盖事故后，政府因此承认了部分真相，但社会的愤慨迫使政府走得更远。
en: His political offensive thwarted, Gorbachev in 1986 embarked on a second subpolicy of

This word, usually translated as “openness” or “publicity,” is in fact a bureaucratic term dating back to Alexander II and signifying officially encouraged notoriety regarding matters the government wishes to see discussed in a critical but constructive fashion. Gorbachev had desired the opening of the system before he came to power; he now made it a priority in order to stimulate the sluggish Party with the sting of criticism. But this policy was soon pushed to unintended lengths by circumstances, the first of which was the Chernobyl disaster in April 1986. This calamity revealed not only that the state of Soviet industry was far worse than the government had suspected, but that the official policy of secrecy perpetuated, indeed aggravated, these disastrous conditions as well as the criminal negligence surrounding them. After initially attempting to cover up the accident, the government therefore admitted a part of the truth, but the indignation of society pressed the government to go further.

zh: 第二个推动局面激进化的新因素是知识分子的态度。作为在勃列日涅夫、苏斯洛夫和安德罗波夫治下受压制最严重的群体，同时也是其才能对松动制度最必要的群体，知识分子起初既对戈尔巴乔夫的改革承诺持谨慎态度，也怀疑他若尝试改革是否具有持久力。切尔诺贝利之后，一些更大胆的知识分子，特别是电影工作者协会的人，在闭门会议上敦促戈尔巴乔夫采取更明确的立场，他们甚至开始自己冒言论风险。1986年中期，戈尔巴乔夫回应道，任命自由派编辑掌管一些莫斯科主要期刊。这些人，特别是《星火》杂志的维塔利·科罗季奇，随后抓住公开性的机会，走得比戈尔巴乔夫预想的更远；但戈尔巴乔夫若想不损害自己改革者的声誉，就无法约束他们。于是，批评的领域逐月扩大；因为对这些六十年代人来说，这是获得自由的最后机会，他们决心充分利用。
en: The second new radicalizing circumstance was the attitude of the intelligentsia. As the group that had been the most stifled under Brezhnev, Suslov, and Andropov, and at the same time the group whose talents were most necessary to limber the system up, the intelligentsia at first was wary of both Gorbachev’s commitment to reform and his staying power if he tried to engage in it. In the wake of Chernobyl, some of the bolder intellectuals, particularly those in the Cinematographers’ Union, pressed Gorbachev in closed meetings to take a clearer stand, and they even started to take verbal risks of their own. In mid-1986 Gorbachev answered by appointing liberal editors to some of the major Moscow periodicals. These men, and in particular Vitalii Korotich of
, then took the bit of

in their teeth and ran with it farther than Gorbachev had intended; but Gorbachev had no way to rein them in without undermining his reputation as a reformer. Thus, month by month the area of criticism expanded; for this was the last chance at freedom for these men of the 1960s, and they were determined to make the most of it.

zh: 尽管如此，人们仍担心这次新解冻会像前一次一样结束，因此在知识分子投身他的事业之前，他们等待着他发出更明确的改革意图信号。而唯一令人信服的信号是释放萨哈罗夫。于是，1986年12月，戈尔巴乔夫让人在高尔基市萨哈罗夫的公寓里安装了一部电话，以便总书记亲自打电话给这位流放者，邀请他回莫斯科。但萨哈罗夫是一个对制度的批评已经超出单纯改革范围的人物；因此，他对改革的支持是战术联盟，而不是加入戈尔巴乔夫的事业。于是，随着他的回归，公开性的调门变得更加尖锐；但这非但没有刺激党务官僚，反而吓坏了他们。
en: Still, apprehension remained that this new thaw would end like its predecessor, and so a clearer signal of reformist intentions was awaited from Gorbachev before the intelligentsia would commit itself to his cause. And the only convincing signal could be the liberation of Sakharov. Accordingly, in December 1986 Gorbachev had a telephone installed in Sakharov’s apartment in Gorky so that the General Secretary could call the exile personally and invite him back to Moscow. But Sakharov was a figure whose criticism of the system had already gone beyond the bounds of mere reform; his support of
, therefore, was a tactical alliance, not an enlistment in Gorbachev’s cause. Thus the tone of
sharpened with his return; but, instead of stimulating the Party apparatchiki, it frightened them.

zh: 当然，公开性的重大主题现在变成了戈尔巴乔夫所谓的苏联历史“空白点”，即斯大林主义。1987年初有两件事，二十多年来第一次重新打开了斯大林问题。第一是电影《忏悔》的公映，该片由谢瓦尔德纳泽的门生、格鲁吉亚导演坚吉兹·阿布拉泽于1984年拍摄。影片以幻影般超现实的手法描绘斯大林时代，同时也具有残酷的现实主义。第二件事是阿纳托利·雷巴科夫一部（平庸的）小说《阿尔巴特街的孩子们》的出版。这部小说以社会主义现实主义的旧式风格写成，至少通过提供一幅斯大林个人肖像，提出了——尽管几乎没有深入探究——一些痛苦的问题。与此同时，一些关于苏联历史的回忆录和解释性文章出现在当时的“厚杂志”上。
en: The great subject of

, of course, now became what Gorbachev called “the blank spots” of Soviet history, or Stalinism. The beginning of 1987 was marked by two events that, for the first time in more than twenty years, reopened the Stalin question. The first was the release of a film,

made in 1984 by a protégé of Shevardnadze, the Georgian director Tengiz Abuladze. The film portrayed the Stalin era in a phantasmagoric and surrealistic idiom that was also brutally realistic. The second event was the publication of a (mediocre) novel by Anatolii Rybakov,

Written in the old-fashioned style of socialist realism, the novel at least raised, though it hardly probed, a few of the painful questions by offering a personal portrait of Stalin. At the same time, a number of memoirs and interpretive articles about Soviet history appeared in the “thick journals” of the periodical press.

zh: 当然，大问题是这一切会走多远？因为公开性不仅是澄清历史记录的努力；正如赫鲁晓夫治下的去斯大林化一样，它也是面对当下问题的努力。然而，它也打开了政权自身合法性的问题；因为制度有一个犯罪的过去，而提出其黑暗起源的问题——即使只是为了纠正弊端——也很容易变成对制度本身的谴责。戈尔巴乔夫及其自由派顾问显然认为，他们可以在批评与摧毁制度之间把握分寸。那些站在制度之外的人，即曾经被监禁的前布鲁诺派，如谢尔盖·格里戈里扬茨，想要彻底揭露制度，为此创办了一份未经审查的杂志《公开性》；萨哈罗夫虽然更谨慎，但离这一立场并不太远。但另一些在1985年还是改革者的人此时惊恐起来，试图遏制——如果不是实际阻止——公开性的威胁洪流。于是，在1987年，社会和党都分裂成阵营。
en: The great question was, of course, how far would all of this go? For

was not just an effort to set the record straight; it was also, as de-Stalinization had been under Khrushchev, an effort to come to terms with the present. However, it also opened the question of the legitimacy of the regime itself; for the system had a criminal past, and to raise the question of its dark origins—even if only to correct abuses—could easily turn into a denunciation of the system itself. Gorbachev and his liberal advisors obviously thought they could walk the fine line between criticism and demolition. Those who stood outside the system, the former Brunos who had once been imprisoned, such as Sergei Grigoriants, wanted to unmask the system completely, and so they founded an uncensored journal,

for this purpose; Sakharov, though more prudent, was not too far from this position. But others who in 1985 had been reformers now took fright and sought to stem, if not actually stop, the threatening flood of
And so in the course of 1987, both society and the Party divided into camps.

zh: 在政治局和书记处层面，此时出现了由谢瓦尔德纳泽、雅科夫列夫和叶利钦组成的左派；围绕政权第二号人物利加乔夫、代表党务机关的右派；以及围绕雷日科夫、代表政府机关并与军工复合体联系在一起的中间派。在这种格局中，戈尔巴乔夫最接近左派，但他仍被迫至少在某些时候、在某些问题上迁就另外两个群体。虽然公开性的程度是这一划分的核心问题，但它也与领导层能够以多大的力度和多快的速度清洗、重组党和国家机关的问题密切相关。
en: At the level of the Politburo and the Secretariat there now emerged a Left of Shevardnadze, Yakovlev, and Yeltsin; a Right around the number two of the regime, Ligachev, who spoke for the Party apparat; and a center around Ryzhkov, who spoke for the government apparat and was associated with the military-industrial complex. In this alignment Gorbachev was closest to the Left, but he nonetheless was compelled to accommodate the other two groups at least some of the time and on some of the issues. Although the degree of

was the central issue in this division, the latter was also intimately related to the question of how far and how fast the leadership would be able to purge and restructure the apparats of both the Party and the state.

zh: 因为在其1986年的公开性运动中，戈尔巴乔夫发现，他改革的工具——党——实际上正是他想要纠正的麻烦的主要根源。此外，他发现自己高估了作为总书记的实际权力。一个1978年才搬到莫斯科的地方政治家，缺乏其前任对中央机器运作的长期经验，戈尔巴乔夫似乎没有意识到莫斯科官僚机构已变得多么根深蒂固，地方官僚机构对上级命令又是多么无动于衷。于是他带着赫鲁晓夫的积极行动开始改革，仿佛忘记了中间二十年已产生官名录政党的迟钝怪物。结果是，在他头两年里，他不断发布命令、更换关键人员，却什么也没有改变。
en: For in the course of his

campaign of 1986, Gorbachev discovered that the instrument of his reform, the Party, was in fact the principal cause of the trouble he wished to correct. In addition, he discovered that he had overestimated his real power as General Secretary. A provincial politician who had moved to Moscow only in 1978 and who lacked the long experience of his predecessors with the workings of the machine at its center, Gorbachev seems to not have realized how incrusted the Muscovite bureaucracy had become, and how unresponsive the local bureaucracies were to commands from the top. So he set about
with the activism of Khrushchev, as if forgetting that the intervening twenty years had produced the lethargic monster of the
Party. The result was that throughout his first two years he issued commands and replaced key personnel, yet nothing changed.

zh: 一位年轻改革者用列宁主义语言的双关总结了1987年：“在二十七大上，我们决定了shto delat，即怎么办，答案是激进经济改革；在六月全会上，我们决定了kak delat，即如何做，答案是经济核算，即为利润定价；在秋天的下一次全会上，我们本应决定s kem delat，即与谁一起做——还有komu delat，即对谁下手——但我们始终没能让那个秋季全会召开。”而这个夭折的剧本确实是戈尔巴乔夫改革的第一套战略：他将利用现有的党——毕竟他是党的老板——作为经济重组的工具。
1986年秋天，当他发现现有党不能这样使用时，他首先用公开性轰炸它。当这不起作用时，他决定通过引入竞争性选举来发动党的普通党员反对机关。这导致了改革的第三个子政策——“民主化”。
en: One young reformer summed up 1987 in a play on Leninist language: “At the Twenty-seventh Party Congress we decided
, or what is to be done, and the answer was radical economic reform; at the June plenum we decided
, or how to do it, and the answer was
, or prices for profit; and at the next plenum, in the fall, we were to decide
, or whom to do it with—and also
, or whom to stick it to—but we could never get that fall plenum to meet.” And this aborted scenario was indeed Gorbachev’s first strategy for
: he would use the existing Party, of which he was, after all, the Boss, as the instrument for economic restructuring.
When in the fall of 1986 he discovered that the existing Party could not be used in this way, he first bombarded it with
And when this did not work, he decided to raise the Party’s rank and file against the apparat by introducing contested elections. This led to the third great subpolicy of
, “democratization.”

zh: 戈尔巴乔夫于1987年1月发起民主化运动，当时他终于能够召开前一年秋天被迫推迟三次的人事问题全会。由于人事变动的愿望仍受挫，他以尖锐批评党的体制作为反击；而且，在一次史无前例的举动中，他让主要讲话电视直播，绕过中央委员会直接向全国呼吁。他宣布“我们需要民主就像需要空气一样”，并提出比导致赫鲁晓夫下台的那些更激进的党章修改：竞争性选举允许多名候选人，以及除最高层少数职位外所有党内职务的五至十五年任期限制。然而，全会拒绝就这些提议采取行动，于是战斗延续到6月的下一次会议。与此同时，第一批攻击现状的重要文章出现在报刊上：瓦西里·谢柳宁揭露了苏联经济统计的问题，尼古拉·什梅廖夫攻击中央计划并主张一定程度的市场化。
en: Gorbachev launched his drive for democratization in January 1987, when he was at last able to convene the plenum on personnel matters that he had had to postpone three times the previous fall. Still frustrated in his desire to make personnel changes, he counterattacked with scathing criticism of the Party as an institution; and, in an unprecedented move, he appealed to the country over the heads of the Central Committee by having his main speech televised. Declaring “we need democracy like air,” he proposed changes in the Party statutes even more radical than those that had led to Khrushchev’s downfall: multiple candidacies for contested elections, and term limits of five to fifteen years for all Party posts except a handful at the very top. The plenum, however, refused to act on these proposals, and so the battle was continued into the next meeting in June. In the meantime, the first major articles attacking the status quo appeared in the press: Vasilii Seliunin demolished Soviet economic statistics, and Nikolai Shmelev attacked central planning and advocated a measure of marketization.

zh: 1987年6月全会标志着戈尔巴乔夫时代第一次突破，走向真正的制度变革。经过两年准备，戈尔巴乔夫的经济专家终于准备好提出比“加速”更多的东西。他们的工作得到全会认可，形成《国有企业法》草案（不久后由最高苏维埃投票通过为法律），该法试图通过规定“自我管理”和“自筹资金”使工业摆脱国家计划委员会和中央各部委的直接控制。这意味着企业此后将在与国家以及彼此之间签订的合同基础上运营；利润可由企业自行决定使用，无论是用于提高工资还是投资；价格政策将“合理化”，信贷将可用于新项目；整个纲领将从1988年1月1日开始，以“逐步”和“审慎”的方式实施。尽管如此，计划和国家部委都没有被废除；因此这场改革仍同以往所有改革一样带有混合性质，尽管比过去任何一次都大胆得多。无数实施细节仍要在实践中制定，这种情况只会在国家和党的机关内部引发持久斗争。尽管如此，僵化的制度已受到重大冲击，现在不可能回到先前的状态。戈尔巴乔夫希望以这种方式逐步使党不再直接监管经济。
en: The June 1987 plenum marked the first breakthrough to real institutional change of the Gorbachev era. After two years of preparation, Gorbachev’s economic experts were at last ready to present something more than “acceleration.” Their work was endorsed by the plenum in a draft Law on State Enterprises (soon after voted as law by the Supreme Soviet), which sought to free industry from the direct control of Gosplan and the central ministries by providing for “self-management” and “self-financing.” This meant that enterprises would henceforth operate on the basis of contracts passed both with the state and among themselves; profits could be used as the enterprises saw fit, whether for increased wages or investment; pricing policy was to be “rationalized,” and credits were to be made available for new ventures; and the whole program was to be implemented beginning January 1, 1988, in a “step by step” and “calibrated” fashion. Still, neither the Plan nor the ministries were abolished; the reform thus remained a hybrid, like all its predecessors, though a much bolder one than any in the past. And innumerable details of implementation remained to be worked out in practice, a circumstance that could only produce a protracted struggle within both the state and the Party apparats. Nonetheless, a major shock had been administered to the stagnant system, and a return to its previous state was now impossible. And in this way Gorbachev hoped to progressively remove the Party from direct supervision of the economy.

zh: 同一时期，其他法律自新经济政策以来首次授权服务业中的小型合作社甚至个人“劳动活动”。这一行动等于使私营企业合法化，尽管此类活动仍必须标为集体或合作社。一些私营企业是原本属于第二经济、如今转入公开经营的单位；另一些则是真正的新创企业；一些从属于这个或那个黑手党；几乎所有企业都依赖国有企业提供原料和销路。民众常常敌视合作社，因为其价格高于国有企业收取的价格，这一事实招致“投机”的指控。到1988年5月合作社运动获得法律地位时，它仍然规模很小，约占经济活动的2%。尽管如此，旧制度再一次受到冲击，个人主动性的空间已被创造出来，而事实证明这个空间越来越难以控制。
en: During this same period, other laws authorized small cooperative and even individual “work activities” in the service sector for the first time since the NEP. This action amounted to the legalization of private enterprise, even though such activity still had to be labeled collective or cooperative. Some of the private enterprises were former units of the second economy that now came out into the open, while others were genuinely new ventures; some were tributary to one or another mafia; and almost all were dependent on state enterprises for raw materials and outlets. The population was often hostile to the cooperatives because their prices were higher than those charged by state enterprises, and this fact invited the charge of “speculation.” By the time the cooperative movement received legal status in May 1988, it was still a very small affair, accounting for approximately 2 percent of economic activity. Nonetheless, once again the old system had been given a shock, and a space for individual initiative had been created that would prove increasingly difficult to control.

zh: 经济改革的第三个方面是，从1987年开始建立苏联机构与外国企业家之间的合资企业。实际上这类企业并非完全新事：菲亚特汽车厂和卡马河卡车厂等大型合办项目已在勃列日涅夫时代实施；而在1920年代，特别是第一个五年计划期间，苏联政府与外国企业签订了重要合同。但所有这些活动都受到政府的密切控制，经济的自给自足性质丝毫没有受到破坏。然而，新的合资企业不同：外国伙伴虽然限于少数股权，但在管理上获得了比苏联历史上任何时候都更大的主动权和更好的利润激励；苏联机构甚至个人被允许享有大得多的自由，不必完全依靠国家便可参与合资企业。结果是国家自给自足状态的一次真正——尽管当时规模有限——的突破，因而也是苏联融入世界市场的一次真正运动。
en: A third aspect of economic

was the creation, beginning in 1987, of joint ventures between Soviet institutions and foreign entrepreneurs. In reality such ventures were not entirely new: Major joint projects, such as the Fiat automobile works and the Kama truck factory, had been undertaken during the Brezhnev era; and in the 1920s, and especially during the First Five-Year Plan, important contracts had been passed between the Soviet government and foreign enterprises. But all of these activities had been closely controlled by the government, and the autarkic nature of the economy had in no way been breached. The new joint ventures, however, were different: the foreign partner, though limited to minority participation, was granted greater initiative in management and better profit incentives than ever before in Soviet history; and Soviet institutions, even individuals, were allowed much greater freedom to enter into ventures independently of the state. The result was a genuine, though at the time modest, breach of national autarky, and thus a real movement towards the Soviet Union’s integration into the world market.

zh: 综合起来，国有企业的新自由、合作社和合资企业构成了自斯大林首次建设社会主义以来最大胆的经济改革纲领。尽管如此，它们仍远未回到新经济政策，因为没有全国市场、没有真实价格、没有自由农民；此外，90%的经济仍归国有，由党的监督下的国家机关直接管理。因此，大问题是这个混合制度中相互冲突的因素能否啮合，还是会把整个结构撕裂。
en: Taken together, the new freedom for state enterprises, the cooperatives, and the joint ventures constituted the boldest program of economic reform since Stalin first built socialism. Still, they fell well short of a return to the NEP, for there was no national market, no real prices, and no free peasantry; moreover, 90 percent of the economy remained nationalized and directly managed by state organs under the Party’s supervision. The great question, therefore, was whether the conflicting elements of this hybrid system could be made to mesh, or whether they would tear the whole structure apart.

zh: 六月全会的最后突破是政治性的：戈尔巴乔夫获得批准，于次年召开一次特别党代表会议。他在一月全会上提出了这一想法，但被否决，因为中央委员会担心这样的集会（实际上是临时党代会）会成为戈尔巴乔夫数月来寻求的中央委员会及其书记处大规模人事变动的场合。他在6月通过承诺这次会议不会被用来进行此类清洗，赢得了对其代表会议的批准。尽管如此，他的目的仍然是振兴党，他试图通过动员基层选举具有改革思想的代表参加代表会议来实现这一目标。一旦该机构召开，总书记将看看能让它批准什么。但决定召开代表会议，导致党内两极分化加剧，并引发了一场长达一年、争夺会议代表构成的活动。
en: The final breakthrough of the June plenum was political: Gorbachev obtained approval for a special Party Conference to be convened the following year. He had put forth this idea at the January plenum, but it had been turned down because the Central Committee feared that such a gathering (in effect an interim Party Congress) would be the occasion for those sweeping personnel changes in the Central Committee and its Secretariat that Gorbachev had been seeking for months. He won approval for his Conference in June by promising that the gathering would not be used for such a purge. Still, his purpose remained a renewed Party, and he sought to achieve this end by mobilizing the base to elect

-minded delegates to the Conference. And once that body had convened, the General Secretary would see what he could get it to approve. But the decision to schedule the Conference resulted in an intensified polarization of the Party and a year-long campaign to control the composition of the gathering.

zh: 1987年秋天，压力主要来自利加乔夫和正统派，他们此时越来越多地被标为“保守派”或“右派”。争论的最大焦点是总书记将在11月革命七十周年之际发表的讲话。自由派知识分子希望与斯大林主义遗产彻底决裂，坦率评价苏联七十年历史；而保守派希望把坦率保持在最低限度，并对政权的过去作出正面评价。面对这些压力，戈尔巴乔夫采取了他此后经常采用的策略：整个秋天，他根据左右两派在特定时刻的相对力量，在两者之间来回摇摆，从而不断占据关键中间地带，使自己在两派之间始终不可或缺。由于保守派当时施加的压力更大，周年讲话的草稿偏向谨慎，这种倾斜引发了改革时代的第一次重大危机。
en: In the fall of 1987 the pressure came primarily from Ligachev and the orthodox, who were now increasingly labeled “conservatives” or the “Right.” The great bone of contention was the speech the General Secretary would deliver in November on the occasion of the seventieth anniversary of the Revolution. The liberal intelligentsia wanted a clean break with the Stalinist heritage and a frank evaluation of seventy years of Soviet history, while the conservatives wished to keep frankness to a minimum and to present a positive balance sheet of the regime’s past. Faced with these pressures, Gorbachev adopted the tactic he would henceforth employ regularly: throughout the fall he tacked back and forth between Right and Left, depending on their relative strength at any given moment, thereby constantly occupying the pivotal middle ground and thus making himself permanently indispensable to both camps. Since the conservatives were exerting the greater pressure at the time, the draft of the anniversary speech leaned in the direction of prudence, and this tilt provoked the first great crisis of the
era.

zh: 在专门审议讲话的十月全会上，鲍里斯·叶利钦——改革者中总是最不耐烦的人——公开攻击利加乔夫和机关是有意义变革的主要障碍。戈尔巴乔夫别无选择，只能拒绝这样大胆的攻击，于是会议以叶利钦的惨败告终。

但这种结局自然而然地把戈尔巴乔夫推向保守派。次月，在有戈尔巴乔夫出席的莫斯科市委会议上，叶利钦受到旧式异端审判，并被解除党内职务。所有改革者都感到沮丧，因为过去的东西仍然如此之多地存留在党的精神和程序中。在随后几个月里，当叶利钦在党报上受到辱骂时，他在人民眼中成了机关手中的殉道者，而戈尔巴乔夫对改革的承诺相应地似乎动摇了。的确，周年讲话令人大失所望：它没有开辟任何新天地，只是谴责斯大林的过激行为，同时为他建设社会主义的功绩辩护。
en: At the October plenum devoted to consideration of the speech, Boris Yeltsin—always the most impatient of the reformers—openly attacked Ligachev and the apparat as the main obstacles to meaningful change. Gorbachev had no choice but to rebuff such a bold assault, and so the meeting ended in a crushing defeat for Yeltsin.

But this denouement automatically pushed Gorbachev towards the conservatives. The next month, at a meeting of the Moscow Party Committee attended by Gorbachev, Yeltsin was subjected to an old-style heresy trial and dismissed from his Party posts. All reformers were dismayed that so much of the past still survived in the Party’s spirit and procedures. As Yeltsin was reviled in the Party press during the ensuing months, in the eyes of the people he appeared a martyr at the hands of the apparat, while Gorbachev’s commitment to reform correspondingly seemed to be wavering. And indeed the anniversary speech was a great disappointment: breaking no new ground, it only deplored Stalin’s excesses while defending his services in building socialism.

zh: 于是跷跷板式的较量持续到1988年春天。3月，利加乔夫和保守派试图发动某种政变，发表了一封由列宁格勒化学教师尼娜·安德烈耶娃写的信。这封信题为《我不能放弃原则》，攻击改革是外来的、颠覆性的，为旧体制作列宁主义和民族主义辩护，同时带有反犹色彩。利加乔夫打算把这场运动推进到什么程度，并不清楚。他可能想推翻戈尔巴乔夫——这些年里每个人心里都有赫鲁晓夫的前例——但至少他是在争取决定党代表会议选举的结果。
自由派知识分子担心公开性可能不久就会被终止，于是团结到戈尔巴乔夫改革周围。戈尔巴乔夫与雅科夫列夫一起，通过发表官方文章驳斥尼娜·安德烈耶娃的立场，给了知识分子所需的领导。在这种两极化的背景下，代表会议代表于6月选出。
en: And so the seesaw contest continued into the spring of 1988. In March, Ligachev and the conservatives attempted a coup of sorts with the publication of a letter by a Leningrad chemistry teacher named Nina Andreeva. Titled “I Cannot Compromise My Principles,” it attacked

as foreign and subversive, and with anti-Semitic overtones it defended the old ways as both Leninist and national. How far Ligachev intended to go with this campaign is not clear. He could have been out to unseat Gorbachev—the precedent of Khrushchev was on everyone’s mind during these years—but at the very least he was seeking to determine the outcome of the elections for the Party Conference.
The liberal intelligentsia, frightened at the prospect that
might soon be ended, rallied to Gorbachev’s

. Together with Yakovlev, Gorbachev gave the intelligentsia the leadership it needed by publishing an official refutation of Nina Andreeva’s positions. And against this polarized background the Conference delegates were elected in June.

zh: 选举结果总体上是机关保守派的胜利；他们不仅赢得了多数代表，而且许多更著名的改革者，如什梅廖夫和扎斯拉夫斯卡娅，遭到引人注目的失败。在这种情况下，不可能对党作出重大改变。但戈尔巴乔夫利用总书记的倡议权和对议程的控制，策划了一场针对代表会议多数的重大反政变。在他的倡议下，会议部分议程通过电视转播，这向全国展示了机关最糟糕的一面。然后，在辩论结束时，戈尔巴乔夫把他事先准备好的“提纲”强行通过代表会议，未经讨论，几乎没有反对声音——这种策略之所以可能，是因为党代会上认可领导层立场的既定习惯。
en: The elections resulted in an overall victory for the apparat conservatives; not only did they win a majority of delegates, but many of the more prominent reformers, such as Shmelev and Zaslavskaia, suffered conspicuous defeats. Under such circumstances there was no possibility of making significant changes in the Party. But Gorbachev, using the General Secretary’s power of initiative and control of the agenda, nonetheless engineered a major countercoup against the Conference majority. On his initiative the proceedings were partially televised, and this served to show the country the apparat at its worst. Then, at the end of the debates, Gorbachev, having prepared his “theses” in advance, railroaded them through the Conference without discussion and with few dissenting voices—a tactic made possible by the established habit at Party Congresses of endorsing the leadership’s position.

zh: 这些提纲规定了一个激进的新民主化阶段。因为戈尔巴乔夫从代表会议代表的选举中确信，他从下面使党民主化的努力已经失败。他现在试图通过复兴苏维埃即行政委员会，在党外创建一个平行的权力基础；苏维埃自1917年以来一直是苏维埃国家名义上的权力机构。他新计划的基石是人民代表大会：其2500名成员由多名候选人中无记名投票选出，每年只开几次短会。这个机构将选举其主席团主席——当然是戈尔巴乔夫本人——作为国家元首或准总统。代表大会还将选举一个由542名成员组成的最高苏维埃，作为国家的常设立法机构。此外，最终还将对所有共和国、省和地方苏维埃及其各自的行政官员进行竞争性选举。虽然苏维埃是提纲的主要主题，但党也没有被遗忘：它同样再次被要求举行竞争性选举，并把党内职务任期限制为两届、最多三届五年任期。
en: These theses provided for a radical new phase of democratization. For Gorbachev had been convinced by the elections of Conference delegates that his efforts to democratize the Party from below had failed. He now sought to create a parallel power base outside the Party by reviving the soviets, or administrative councils, which since 1917 had been the nominal power in the Soviet state. The cornerstone of his new plan was a Congress of People’s Deputies: Its 2,500 members, chosen by secret ballot from among multiple candidates, would meet only for short periods a few times each year. This body would elect a chairman of its Presidium—Gorbachev himself, of course—who would function as head of state, or quasi president. The Congress would also elect a Supreme Soviet of 542 members that would function as the standing legislature of the country. In addition, there would eventually be contested elections for all of the republican, provincial, and local soviets, as well as for their respective executive officers. Although the soviets were the main subject of the theses, the Party was not forgotten: it, too, was again summoned to hold contested elections and to limit tenure in Party offices to two or at the most three five-year terms.
