zh: 此外，苏维埃和党都要把苏联转变为“基于法治的社会主义国家”，这是对 sotsialisticheskoe pravovoe gosudarstvo 通常的累赘译法。但戈尔巴乔夫及其理论家如鲍里斯·库拉什维利的意思，最好表述为社会主义法治国（Rechtsstaat），用这个最熟悉的术语来表示孟德斯鸠所谓与任意专制相对的法治国（état de droit）。这种制度重新定义有两个动机：戈尔巴乔夫和改革者真诚地相信法治对于人的尊严是必要的，因而对于使苏联成为国际社会文明成员也是必要的；他们还相信，法治对于提高政府效率和公民责任感是必要的。但大问题是，一直凌驾于法律之上的党国是否有能力进行这样的转变，还是试图使它服从法律只会把它撕裂。
en: Both the soviets and the Party, moreover, were to transform the Soviet Union into a “socialist state based on the rule of law,” to use the usual cumbersome translation of
. But what Gorbachev and his theorists, such as Boris Kurashvili, meant is best rendered as a socialist
, to use the most familiar term for what Montesquieu had called an é

as opposed to an arbitrary despotism. There were two motives for this redefinition of the system: Gorbachev and the reformers genuinely believed that the rule of law was necessary for human dignity, and thus for making the Soviet Union a civilized member of the international community; they also believed that it was necessary to promote efficiency in government and responsibility among the citizens. But the great question was whether the Party-state, which had always been above the law, was capable of such a transformation, or whether the attempt to subject it to law would simply tear it apart.

zh: 当各省第一书记在代表会议前的秘密会议上听取这些真正革命性的提议时，他们反对说，戈尔巴乔夫的计划将给非党机构太多权力，特别是在他们自己的地方势力范围内。于是在提纲的最终草案中，戈尔巴乔夫规定，任何地区的第一书记也必须竞选相应苏维埃的主席，就像他本人将竞选“总统”一样。然而后来，当第一书记们看到选举将是真实的、因而危险时，他们又转回党和苏维埃职能分离。但无论如何，党务机关陷入了两难，因为无论哪种方式，它都将受到自1918年以来闻所未闻的民众控制和公共问责。而这确实是整个行动的意义所在：戈尔巴乔夫希望通过让党对其表现向全国负责，来振兴党并更新其干部。
en: When provincial First Secretaries were briefed on these truly revolutionary proposals in a confidential meeting before the Conference, they objected that Gorbachev’s scheme would give too much power to non-Party bodies, particularly in their own provincial bailiwicks. So in the final draft of his theses Gorbachev stipulated that the First Secretary of any given region would also have to stand for election as chairman of the corresponding soviet, just as he himself would stand for election as “president.” Later, however, when the First Secretaries saw that the elections were intended to be real, and therefore dangerous, they switched back to a separation of Party and soviet functions. But in any event the apparat was caught, because either way, it would be subject to popular control and public accountability in a manner unknown since 1918. And this indeed was the whole point of the operation: Gorbachev wished to rejuvenate the Party and renew its cadres by making it answerable to the country for its performance.

zh: 代表会议之后，戈尔巴乔夫着手直接攻击机关。1988年9月，在仍然神秘的情况下，他对机关的最高层——书记处和政治局保守派——发动了一场名副其实的政变。莫斯科军区秘密进入戒备状态，并于当月最后一天召开紧急全会。谢瓦尔德纳泽显然没有事先得到这次会议的通知，他刚抵达纽约联合国就被召回。全会仅持续一小时，结束时利加乔夫被调到书记处一个较低职位，尽管他仍留在政治局。他的盟友切布里科夫也被调离，由弗拉基米尔·克留奇科夫取代为克格勃首脑，尽管切布里科夫也仍留在政治局。葛罗米柯和另外三名勃列日涅夫留任者从该机构退休。更重要的是，书记处工作人员被削减约40%，从而大大限制了机关监督国家和经济官僚机构的能力。次日，最高苏维埃奉命接受葛罗米柯辞去其主席团主席即“总统”职务，并选举戈尔巴乔夫担任该职——这是他第一次获得党的等级体系之外的职位。
en: In the wake of the Conference, Gorbachev proceeded to attack the apparat directly. During September 1988, in circumstances that still remain mysterious, he carried out a veritable coup d’état against the summit of the apparat, the Secretariat and the Politburo conservatives. The Moscow military district was secretly put on alert, and an emergency plenum was called for the last day of the month. Shevardnadze, who clearly had no advance notice of this meeting, was summoned back from the United Nations in New York where he had just arrived. The plenum lasted a mere hour, and when it was over Ligachev had been shunted aside to a lesser post in the Secretariat, though he remained on the Politburo. His ally, Chebrikov, was also shunted aside and replaced as head of the KGB by Vladimir Kriuchkov, though Chebrikov, too, remained on the Politburo. Gromyko and three other Brezhnev holdovers were retired from that body. Even more important, the staff of the Secretariat was cut back by some 40 percent, thereby significantly limiting the apparat’s ability to monitor the state and economic bureaucracies. The next day the Supreme Soviet, on command, accepted Gromyko’s resignation as chairman or “president” of its Presidium and elected Gorbachev to that post-the first time he acquired an office outside the Party hierarchy.

zh: 这场九月政变就这样以极大的力度把党排除在对国家的直接管理之外，但它采取的方式非常符合党传统的专断和任意作风。这场政变还具有另一重矛盾，因为戈尔巴乔夫在尚未通过复兴苏维埃体系建立新的治理机构之前，就在拆除旧的政府机构。这使改革在政治上如同在经济上一样，悬在两个世界之间。随着民主化变成总书记对自己党发动的一种战争，戈尔巴乔夫显然已决定“破釜沉舟”，正如当时一位身处要津的改革者所说。
en: This September coup thus took the Party out of direct management of the country with a vengeance, but it did so very much in the Party’s traditional autocratic and arbitrary manner. The coup was ambiguous in still another way, for Gorbachev was dismantling his old apparatus of government before he had created a new one in the form of a revived system of soviets. And this left

suspended between two worlds in politics just as it was in economics. With democratization having become a form of warfare waged by the General Secretary against his own Party, Gorbachev had clearly decided “to go for broke,” as one well-placed reformer put it at the time.

zh: 为什么戈尔巴乔夫在国内事务上起初如此谨慎，现在却以他在1986年雷克雅未克外交政策中表现出的同样鲁莽来处理这些问题？部分答案必定是，经过两年与机关阻挠的斗争，他对机关的愤怒不断增长。另一部分答案是他那种彻头彻尾共产主义的领袖角色观。作为列宁的党之首，他必须成为党当前的斗争——反对“停滞”的斗争——中的当代列宁。而在这个角色中，他必须彻底革命。然而，他的革命列宁主义也必须是一种现代化且在国际上体面的列宁主义。因此，党的领袖职位必须与一个依照民主程序和法律选举产生的“总统”职位结合起来。这种从未明确说出的想法，显然隐含在戈尔巴乔夫实施“民主化”纲领的方式中：他始终平衡自己作为党和苏维埃两个体系首脑的含糊甚至相互冲突的角色，不断煽动后一体系反对前一体系——但从不过分。正如一位苏联政治学家所说，戈尔巴乔夫始终拿不定主意，自己是路德还是教皇。
en: Why should Gorbachev, initially so prudent in domestic matters, now deal with those problems with the same recklessness he had shown with his foreign policy in 1986 at Reykjavik? A part of the answer must be his mounting anger with the apparat after two years of struggling with its obstructionism. Another part of the answer is his thoroughly Communist concept of his role as leader. As the head of the Party of Lenin, he had to be the Lenin of his day in the Party’s latest struggle, the struggle against “stagnation.” And in this role he had to be thoroughly revolutionary. Yet his revolutionary Leninism also had to be a modernized and internationally respectable one. Thus the post of Party leader had to be combined with that of a democratically and legally elected “president.” Such thinking, never explicitly spelled out, was clearly implicit in the way Gorbachev implemented his program of “democratization”: he always balanced his own ambiguous, indeed conflicting, roles as head of both the Party and the Soviet systems, constantly inciting the latter system against the former—but never too much. As one Soviet political scientist put it, Gorbachev never could make up his mind whether he was Luther or the Pope.

zh: 那么，具体而言，他期望通过这种不寻常的安排实现什么？他并不是要引入西方式民主，甚至也不是当时人们常假设、他后来声称是自己目标的“市场社会主义”。他寻求的是通过经过革新、但仍主要处于他个人领导之下的苏维埃，动员改革的所有支持者；而改革，当然是指他自己的纲领，即一种现代化、更人道、更高效的社会主义，大致就是到1988年已显露的那个纲领。
en: And what, concretely, did he expect to accomplish with this unusual arrangement? He was not out to introduce Western-style democracy or even “market socialism,” as was often assumed at the time and which he later claimed were his goals. He sought, rather, to mobilize all of the supporters of
through renovated soviets that would remain very much under his personal leadership; and
, of course, meant his own program for a modernized, more humane, and more efficient socialism, pretty much as this program had been revealed by 1988.

zh: 这些改革的忠诚拥护者将主要来自党内，大概是较年轻、受教育较好的党员，但也会来自有远见的非党干部；这两个群体合在一起，将为即将到来的苏维埃选举组成“人民阵线”。正如戈尔巴乔夫在1989年1月对选举的界定，它们不会是“某种自发过程”，而是“一场极其重要的群众运动，其成功可以通过高度的组织和责任感来保证”，同时避免诸如“集团自私、傲慢和政治投机主义的表现”这类“消极现象”。他总结说，“党组织必须在所有这些问题上采取明确、有原则的立场。”
换言之，新的人民代表大会实质上将是一个更开放的平行党，或一个国家复兴的共同阵线。但要做到这种程度的改组，旧党必须被搁置，甚至部分被拆解；鉴于党国的性质，这只能是一项危险的手术。
en: These

loyalists would come largely from the Party and presumably be its younger and better-educated members, but they would also come from the forward-looking non-Party cadres; and the two groups together would form “popular fronts” for the forthcoming soviet elections. As Gorbachev defined the elections in January 1989, they would not be “some kind of spontaneous process,” but rather “a highly important mass campaign, the success of which can be ensured by a high degree of organization and responsibility,” avoiding such “negative phenomena” as “manifestations of group selfishness, arrogance, and political careerism.” He concluded that “Party organizations must take clear-cut, principled positions on all these questions.”

In other words, the new Congress of People’s Deputies was to be in essence a more open, parallel Party, or a common front for national renewal. But to achieve this degree of restructuring the old Party had to be sidelined, indeed partially dismantled; and given the nature of the Party-state, this could only be a dangerous operation.

zh: 当时，各种苏联评论家和外国外交官指出了这一战略与斯大林清洗之间的相似之处——尽管手段不同，两位领导人都寻求类似的政治结果。斯大林曾利用一个平行的权力基础，即扩大并完善的内务人民委员部（NKVD），来拆解旧党并给自己造一个新党，而这正是戈尔巴乔夫试图用复兴的苏维埃来完成的事。戈尔巴乔夫的策略还有另一个先例，即毛泽东的文化大革命：在这场奇异的行动中，失去对机关控制却仍保有领袖光环的党首，发动年轻的红卫兵和军队单位去摧毁那个党，以便创建一个献身于不断革命的新党。同样，方法和目标与戈尔巴乔夫大不相同，但政治行动的结构相近。的确，赫鲁晓夫的去斯大林化在其时代语境中与戈尔巴乔夫的民主化一样革命，它也是由最高领导人对领导层多数发动一场类似政变的行动而启动的。这一切说明，戈尔巴乔夫尽管渴望使共产主义现代化和西方化，仍然是一个按照只能通过自上而下的革命来变革的制度的动力行事的党首。
en: At the time, various Soviet commentators and foreign diplomats pointed out the similarities between this strategy and Stalin’s purges—although the means were different, both leaders sought similar political results. Stalin had used a parallel power base, an enlarged and perfected NKVD, to dismantle the old Party and give himself a new one, and this is just what Gorbachev was attempting to accomplish with his revived soviets. There is still another precedent for Gorbachev’s strategy, namely Mao Zedong’s Cultural Revolution: in this fantastic operation, the head of the Party, who had lost control of his apparat and yet retained his aura as Leader, raised up youthful Red Guards and army units to destroy that Party in order to create a new one devoted to permanent revolution. Again, the methods and the goal are quite different from those of Gorbachev, but the structure of the political action is close. Indeed, Khrushchev’s de-Stalinization, in the context of its time as revolutionary as Gorbachev’s democratization, was initiated as a kind of coup d’état by the Boss against the majority of the leadership. All of which is to say that Gorbachev, for all his desire to modernize and Westernize Communism, was still a Party chief operating in terms of the dynamic of a system that can change only by revolution from above.

en: REVOLUTION FROM BELOW

zh: 到1988年底，戈尔巴乔夫自上而下的革命触发了另一场革命——可以说是来自侧翼的革命，发生在知识分子中间。这场革命反过来又启动了社会大众中自下而上的革命。而这两场革命都是公开性意料之外的结果。
en: By the end of 1988 Gorbachev’s revolution from above had triggered another revolution-one from the side, so to speak, among the intelligentsia. This revolution in turn started a revolution from below, in society at large. And both of these revolutions were the unintended fruits of

zh: 一旦去斯大林化问题在1987年初重新提出，知识分子便向前推进，先是在厚杂志上，最终在电视上，重新审视整个苏联过去，把它当作改变当下的不可或缺前奏。这一过程使1987—1988年成为公开性的伟大时期：一连串揭露远远超出赫鲁晓夫解冻时期所发生的，并永久改变了民族意识。戈尔巴乔夫1987年11月的周年讲话在所有重要问题上含糊其辞，结果并未起到威慑作用：编辑催逼审查者，作者催逼编辑，公众又催逼两者，于是一个又一个禁忌倒下。萨米兹达特公开出现，塔米兹达特回到国内。诸如《日瓦戈医生》这样的禁书经典终于合法问世，弗拉基米尔·纳博科夫等流亡作家的作品也是如此。
en: Once the issue of de-Stalinization had been reopened in early 1987, the intelligentsia pressed forward, first in the thick journals and ultimately on television, with a reexamination of the whole Soviet past as the indispensable prelude to changing things in the present. This process made 1987-1988 the great period of

: a cascade of revelations went far beyond what had occurred during Khrushchev’s thaw and permanently changed the national consciousness. The fact that Gorbachev’s anniversary speech of November 1987 had hedged on all of the important issues turned out to have no deterrent effect: editors pressed the censors, and authors pressed the editors, and the public pressed both, and as a consequence one taboo after another fell.

1930年代的清洗审判被正式宣布为捏造，当时所有反对派人物——除托洛茨基外——都获得平反。布哈林的一些著作被重印；第一次出版的是他在被捕前夕口授给妻子的遗书，其中申明他对革命原则的忠诚。（然而，这份文件削弱了围绕布哈林的神话，因为它揭示，在1930年之后的“七年”里，即整个斯大林主义盛期，他与党的路线并无分歧。
）西方苏联学研究也被引入帮助填补空白点：斯蒂芬·科恩的布哈林传记出了译本，罗伯特·康奎斯特的《大恐怖》也是如此。
en: The first area to be opened was the high Stalinism of the 1930s. Andrei Platonov’s

. Vasilii Grossman’s
, which in 1961 Suslov had said could not be published in less than two hundred to three hundred years, presented Hitler and Stalin as kindred figures.

The purge trials of the 1930s were officially declared to be fraudulent, and all of the opposition figures of that time—with the exception of Trotsky—were rehabilitated. Some of Bukharin’s works were reprinted; and published for the first time was the testament-letter, dictated to his wife on the eve of his arrest, which affirmed his fidelity to the principles of the Revolution. (This document, however, undercut the myth surrounding Bukharin by revealing that he had no disagreement with the Party line during the “seven years” after 1930, that is, throughout the period of high Stalinism.

zh: 斯大林的恐怖当然引出了他的制度整体性质的问题。这首先意味着集体化，鲍里斯·莫扎耶夫的《庄稼汉与婆娘》（Muzhiki i Baby）对那场事件的恐怖作了相当准确的描绘。
但集体化又引出斯大林强制工业化的问题，从而引出他的一般统治方法。在这个问题上，亚历山大·别克的《新任命》具有特别重要的意义：这部小说多年前在西方出版，1987年在俄罗斯出版；它讲述一个斯大林主义工业管理者的故事，后来成为加夫里尔·波波夫——后来第一位后共产主义莫斯科市长——一篇文章的主题，波波夫在文中把斯大林主义分析为“行政—命令制度”。
“行政”一词是苏联对“强制和独裁”的旧委婉语，而如前所述，“命令”借自西方术语“命令经济”；复合形容词“行政—命令”是“极权主义”的替代词，后者直到1990年才能在俄罗斯公开使用。
波波夫这个笨拙的新词立即成为对原初斯大林主义及其延续至今的普遍接受的称呼。
en: Stalin’s terror, of course, raised the question of the nature of his system as a whole. This meant, first, collectivization, and Boris Mozhaiev’s
) gave a reasonably accurate picture of the horrors of that event.
But collectivization in turn raised the question of Stalin’s forced industrialization, and thus of his general method of government. On this subject Aleksandr Bek’s novel

), published years earlier in the West and in 1987 in Russia, was of special importance: The story of a Stalinist industrial manager, it became the subject of an essay by Gavriil Popov, later the first post-Communist mayor of Moscow, in which he analyzed Stalinism as the “administrative-command system.”

The term “administrative” was the old Soviet euphemism for “coercive and dictatorial,” and, as already noted, “command” was adapted from the Western term “command economy”; and the compound adjective “administrative-command” was a substitute for “totalitarian,” a term that could not be used openly in Russia until 1990.
Popov’s cumbersome neologism immediately became the generally accepted designation of both original Stalinism and its prolongation into the present.

zh: 但如果这就是制度的性质，那么接下来要探讨的主题就是制度的起源和斯大林主义的替代方案。因为公开性的历史调查目的不仅是澄清记录：它是为了发现过去哪里出了错，以便在当下纠正。作为这一过程的一部分，赫鲁晓夫在二十五年间被当作不存在的人，现在获得平反。
但更重要的是追问制度原初的错误究竟在哪里。瓦西里·谢柳宁在1988年初以《起源》一文开启了这一主题，他认为麻烦的根源部分在于俄罗斯的威权传统，但更在于最大主义社会主义的乌托邦主义；谢柳宁甚至提出列宁对“资产阶级”市场力量的教条式敌视是问题的一个促成因素这一微妙问题。
亚历山大·齐普科更加明确地归咎于马克思和马克思主义对市场的敌视：马克思主义使经济发展的威权方法几乎不可避免。
针对齐普科，伊戈尔·克利亚姆金主张，是俄罗斯的落后以及伊凡雷帝和彼得大帝的专制传统产生了斯大林主义，从而贬低了布哈林替代方案——但并没有为斯大林辩护，实际上把斯大林的政策解释为一种粗陋的现代化形式。
en: But if this was the nature of the system, then the next topics to be explored were the origin of the system and the alternatives to Stalinism. For the purpose of the historical inquest of

was not just to set the record straight: it was an effort to discover where things went wrong in the past so that they might be set aright in the present. As a part of this process, Khrushchev, for twenty-five years a nonperson, was rehabilitated.

But much more important was the inquiry into the location of the original sin of the system. Vasilii Seliunin opened this subject in early 1988 with an article titled “Origins,” which saw the source of the trouble in part in the Russian authoritarian tradition, but even more in the utopianism of maximalist socialism; Seliunin even went so far as to raise the delicate question of Lenin’s doctrinaire hostility to the “bourgeois” forces of the market as a contributory factor in the problem.
Aleksandr Tsipko was even more emphatic in blaming Marx and Marxist hostility to the market: Marxism made an authoritarian method of economic development almost unavoidable.

In response to Tsipko, Igor Kliamkin contended that it was Russian backwardness and the autocratic tradition of Ivan the Terrible and Peter the Great that had produced Stalinism, thus discounting the Bukharin alternative—but without justifying Stalin, whose policies were in effect explained as a crude form of modernization.

zh: 因此，到人民代表大会前夕，从战时共产主义到勃列日涅夫的整个苏联历史都已开放重新评价，对这场悲剧的基本解释模式至少已被提出。然而，某些禁忌仍然存在。首先，除了谢柳宁的暗示外，列宁仍然不可触碰。同样，党的积极作用不能质疑，尽管列宁之后大多数党的领导人都被官方承认基本上犯了错误。社会主义秩序的根本健全性也不能质疑，尽管市场的某些优点现在得到承认。最后，仍然不可能出版公开违反这些禁忌的作者；这意味着索尔仁尼琴直到1990年仍被禁止。尽管如此，去神秘化进程已走得如此之远，最后一些禁忌的倒下只是时间和环境的问题。
en: And so by the eve of the Congress of People’s Deputies the whole of Soviet history from War Communism to Brezhnev had been opened up for reevaluation, and the basic modes of explanation of the tragedy had at least been suggested. Certain taboos, however, still remained. First, except for Seliunin’s hints, Lenin remained untouchable. Similarly, the positive role of the Party could not be questioned, even though most of its leaders after Lenin were officially recognized as having been basically in error. Nor could the fundamental soundness of the socialist order be questioned, even though certain merits of the market were now acknowledged. Finally, it was still not possible to publish authors who openly violated these taboos; and this meant that Solzhenitsyn remained forbidden until 1990. Still, the process of demystification had gone so far that it was only a matter of time and circumstances before the last taboos would fall.

zh: 于是，本意是使制度恢复活力的公开性，实际上通过使维系制度的种种神话失去信誉而削弱了制度。起初只是填补斯大林时代事实空白点的有限过程，变成了一股坦率的洪流：不仅斯大林和勃列日涅夫漫长几十年的神话被一扫而空，而且苏维埃主义的基础本身——马克思的经济理论，甚至列宁的政治实践——都失去了信誉。到1988年，马克思列宁主义已是一片废墟，最激进改革者之一、历史学家尤里·阿法纳西耶夫公开谴责它妨碍清醒思考，若国家要以任何有意义的方式改组，就必须抛弃它。
en: Thus

, which had been intended to revivify the system, had in fact undermined it by discrediting the myths that sustained it. What had begun as a limited process of filling in factual blank spots of the Stalin era had led to a flood of candor in which not only were the myths of the long decades of Stalin and Brezhnev swept away, but the very foundations of Sovietism—the economic theories of Marx and even the political practices of Lenin—were discredited. By 1988 Marxism-Leninism was a shambles, and the historian Iurii Afanasiev, one of the most radical of all the reformers, openly denounced it as an obstacle to clear thinking that had to be discarded if the country were to be restructured in any meaningful way.

zh: 于是，在两年内，一丝公开性就摧毁了七十年的意识形态工作。1920年代锻造的“木头语言”、1930年代的社会主义现实主义、把现实描绘成无尽阶级斗争的形象——全都悄然消散，人们在讨论真实问题时恢复了正常语言。因为每一条关于过去罪行和当下灾难的新揭露，与其说激励人民为改革作出新努力，不如说使制度本身在他们眼中失去神圣性；而且由于神话早在1970年代某个时候就已消亡，尤其是在年轻人中间，这种去神圣化进行得更加彻底。相应地，双重思想中现实的一半赶走了意识形态的一半，被压抑的对谎言的意识如洪水般公开涌现。这种合法性的丧失将证明对制度是致命的，因为其超现实的结构使它们无法在真相曝光后存活。于是，一个诞生于意识形态的政权，在那一意识形态灭绝后便开始崩溃。或者，正如一句俄罗斯谚语所说：死鱼从头烂起。
en: And so in two years a whiff of

had demolished the ideological work of seven decades. The “wooden language” forged in the 1920s, the socialist realism of the 1930s, the image of reality as endless class war—all simply faded away, and people reverted to the use of normal speech in discussing their real problems. For each new revelation about past crimes and present disasters did less to stimulate the people to new efforts on behalf of

than to desacralize the system as such in their eyes; it did so all the more thoroughly since the Myth had expired some time in the 1970s, especially among the young. Accordingly, the realistic half of doublethink drove out the ideological half, and the repressed awareness of the Lie poured out into the open in a flood. This loss of legitimacy would prove fatal to the system, for its surreal structures were such that they could not survive exposure to the truth. Thus, a regime born of ideology started to collapse once that ideology was extinct. Or, as a Russian proverb has it: A dead fish rots from the head.

zh: 这种意识形态解释与共产主义危机始于1970年代末经济衰退的论点并不矛盾。尽管这种衰退千真万确，但它本身并未推翻政权。在一个正常制度中，经济危机只会导致新的发展战略；它不一定意味着要改换成另一种制度。然而，在意识形态专政的苏联世界中，经济衰退破坏了制度的一个不可或缺的神话，即社会主义作为一种生产方式从长远看优于资本主义。在1930年代大萧条期间，以及第二次世界大战后约十五年的重建时期，苏联社会主义不会有一天比资本主义表现更好，并非显而易见。然而到1985年，在四十年和平时期为苏联恢复提供条件之后，对经济“力量对比”的真实趋势已不可能抱有任何幻想。只要苏联仍与西方隔绝，这种衰退就能被掩盖。但当1960年代和1970年代精英成员能够访问西方时，意识形态幻想开始崩解；而当公开性下终于向大众播出了接近真相的东西时，这些幻想彻底崩溃。于是，经济失败产生的远不止物质危机；它使苏维埃主义的整体受到质疑，并暗示应当改换成另一种制度。现有制度下一切“光明未来”的承诺都失去信誉；制度的当下失败，连同其犯罪的过去，加起来就是“在一条通向虚无的路上走了七十年”，这是到1989年初人们越来越常听到的说法。
en: This ideological explanation is not in contradiction with the thesis that the crisis of Communism began with the economic decline of the late 1970s. Although this decline was all too real, it did not by itself bring down the regime. In a normal system, economic crisis simply leads to new strategies of development; it does not necessarily imply changing to another kind of system. In the ideocratic Soviet world, however, the economic decline acted to destroy an indispensable myth of the system, namely that socialism in the long run is superior to capitalism as a mode of production. During the Great Depression of the 1930s, and then in the fifteen or so years of reconstruction following; the Second World War, it was not prima facie obvious that Soviet socialism would not someday perform better than capitalism. By 1985, however, after forty years of peace had permitted a Soviet recovery, no illusion was possible about the real trend of the economic “correlation of forces.” So long as the Soviet Union had remained cut off from the West, this decline could be concealed. But when, in the 1960s and 1970s, members of the elite could visit the West, ideological illusions began to crumble; and when, under

something approximating the truth was finally broadcast to the population at large, these illusions collapsed completely. Thus the economic failure produced much more than a material crisis; it called into question the totality of Sovietism and implied that change to another kind of system was in order. All promises of a “radiant future” under the existing system were discredited; the system’s present failure, in conjunction with its criminal past, added up to “seventy years on the road to nowhere,” as one increasingly heard by the beginning of 1989.

zh: 那么，为什么政权明知二十年前勃列日涅夫粉碎布拉格之春正是因为捷克斯洛伐克人着手废除审查制度，却仍要承担公开性的风险？他们这样做，部分是因为若要震动命令—行政制度以复兴经济并保住国家超级大国地位，他们别无选择：不可能有一个充满活力却拥有被动无知人口的经济。此外，他们相信制度已变得如此“腐朽”，必须来一次快速休克：正如雅科夫列夫1989年初在对党的干部的一次内部讲话中所说：“我们大概只有两三年时间来证明列宁主义社会主义能够运作。”
他们承担公开性风险还因为，正如持不同政见者谢尔盖·格里戈里扬茨所观察到的，这些党务官僚对他们所统治的社会简直一无所知：正如戈尔巴乔夫后来在1990年承认的，“当我们开始时，我们并不了解我们所面临问题的深度。”
于是，最后一位想当“当代列宁”的人，跌跌撞撞地成了政权末期的魔法师学徒。
en: So why did the regime take the risk of

when its leaders knew full well that twenty years earlier Brezhnev had crushed the Prague Spring precisely because the Czechoslovaks had moved to abolish censorship? They did so in part because they had no choice if they were to shake up the command-administrative system in order to revive the economy and preserve the country’s superpower status: it was impossible to have a dynamic economy with a passive and ignorant population. Furthermore, they believed the system had become so “rotten” that a rapid shock was necessary: as Yakovlev put it in a confidential speech to Party cadres in early 1989: “We probably have no more than two or three years to prove that Leninist socialism can work.”
They took the risk of

also because, as the dissident Sergei Grigoriants observed, these apparatchiki were simply uninformed regarding the society they ruled: as Gorbachev was to admit in 1990, “When we started, we did not understand the depth of the problems we faced.”
And so the last would-be “Lenin of today” stumbled into a career of fin-de-régime sorcerer’s apprentice.

它们独立于党，就某个社会问题成立，通常以地方或地区为基础，针对党忽视问题或自身造成问题的领域。它们的起源常常是生态威胁，如贝加尔湖污染或波罗的海国家的核电站；有时出发点是保护历史纪念物，如诗人叶赛宁自杀身亡的列宁格勒旅馆，或莫斯科某座因建旅馆而受威胁的中世纪教堂。但由于这些团体必须向党施压，它们很快转向政治：到1987年初，支持改革的俱乐部已经出现，其中许多在名称中加入“民主改革”一词，以强调虽然他们希望在制度内工作，但也会把改革推得比政权预想的更远。到1987年底，这些俱乐部已组成全联盟社会主义俱乐部联合会。
en: The intelligentsia’s revolution from the side soon became a people’s revolution from below. The years 1987-1988 saw a proliferation of self-organized “informal” associations, the

Independent of the Party, they were created to address one or another social problem, usually on a local or regional basis, in areas where the Party had been remiss or was actively at fault. Very often their origin was in threats to the ecology, such as the pollution of Lake Baikal or the nuclear power plants of the Baltic states; at times their point of departure was a concern for preserving historical monuments, such as the Leningrad hotel where the poet Esenin had committed suicide, or certain medieval churches threatened by the construction of a hotel in Moscow. But since these groups had to pressure the Party, they soon moved on to politics: By early 1987 clubs in support
had appeared, and many of these put the term “democratic

” in their name to emphasize that, though they wished to work within the system, they would also push reform farther than the regime intended. By late 1987 these clubs had formed an All-Union Federation of Socialist Clubs.

zh: 但其他活动家得出结论，制度已无可救药地“极权”，改革只是党的又一场骗局，唯一的解决办法是向宪政民主秩序过渡。1988年5月，这些活动家组成了他们所谓的政党——民主联盟。他们的纲领当然不是积极革命，因为那将毫无希望；相反，他们寻求利用复兴的苏维埃制度推进二月革命原则而非十月革命原则，从而为制度的逐步清算铺路。当这个团体的年轻人在1988年夏天经常聚集的莫斯科普希金广场或列宁格勒喀山大教堂前向人群高谈阔论时，惊讶的观察者把他们视为边缘怪人。尽管他们及其志同道合者格里戈里扬茨不时遭到克格勃殴打，但一年之内，建制派自由派私下里已同意他们的观点；三年之内，叶利钦将凭借相当于他们纲领的主张当选俄罗斯总统。
en: But other activists concluded that the system was hopelessly “totalitarian,” that

was just another Party fraud, and that the only solution was a transition to a constitutional democratic order. And in May 1988, these activists formed what they called a political party, the Democratic Union. Their program, of course, was not active revolution, since that would be hopeless; rather, they sought to use the revived soviet system to further the principles of the February Revolution over those of October, and thus to prepare the way for the gradual liquidation of the system. As young men from this group held forth before the crowds that by the summer of 1988 regularly gathered on Pushkin Square in Moscow or before the Kazan Cathedral in Leningrad, amazed observers regarded them as marginal cranks. Although they and their kindred spirit, Grigoriants, were periodically roughed up by the KGB, within a year their opinions were secretly shared by establishment liberals, and within three years Yeltsin would be elected president of Russia on the equivalent of their program.

zh: 到1988年，各种“非正式”团体合在一起被称为“公民社会”，这个词当年从波兰输入，那里独立于党国的社会力量现象可追溯到KOR和团结工会。这是自最后一个公民社会——独立农民——在1930年被粉碎以来，俄罗斯第一次出现类似的社会力量。然而，这种社会自主性的复兴也有另一面。一些反民主的社会运动也出现了，特别是“纪念”（Pamiat）。它从保护莫斯科旧教堂的运动中生长出来，却发展成一个极端威权主义、民族主义和反犹的组织。尽管它在国外备受关注，在俄罗斯的重要性却不大：在随后两年的全国和地方选举中，它没有一名候选人当选，而源自民主非正式团体的组织有数千名候选人获胜，并在叶利钦领导下接管了政府。
en: Taken together, the various kinds of “informals” were by 1988 known as “civil society,” a term imported in that year from Poland, where the phenomenon of a social force independent of the Party-state went back to KOR and Solidarity. This was the first time a similar social force had existed in Russia since the last civil society, that of the independent peasantry, was crushed in 1930. There was, however, a reverse side to this renascence of social autonomy. A few antidemocratic social movements appeared as well, notably Pamiat, or Memory. It had grown out of the movement to preserve Moscow’s old churches, hut it developed into a stridently authoritarian, nationalistic, and anti-Semitic organization. Although it received much attention abroad, its importance in Russia was not great: in the elections of the next two years, at both the national and local levels, it failed to place a single candidate in office, whereas organizations growing out of the democratic
saw thousands of their candidates victorious and under Yeltsin took over the government.

en: THE REVOLT OF THE NATIONALITIES

zh: 因为少数民族是戈尔巴乔夫不熟悉的苏联现实的另一方面。

从斯大林起，他所有前任都有在边疆地区统治的直接经验，懂得如何软硬兼施，使当地保持平静。然而，戈尔巴乔夫缺乏这种经验，似乎相信勃列日涅夫时期形成的官方立场，即各民族已融合成一个真正的“苏联人民”，忠诚于“联盟”作为其经济发展和国际安全的载体。因此，他们只需一点“改组”，按“中心”对该词的理解。然而实际上，各民族共和国遭受着与戈尔巴乔夫在党内遇到的同一种结构性停滞和制度僵化，再加上族群不满。而对领导层来说完全出乎意料，这个问题很快成为导致制度垮台的三大因素之一——与经济失败和意识形态失色并列。为解释这一重大问题，有必要简要回顾过去。
en: For the minority nationalities were another aspect of Soviet reality with which Gorbachev was unacquainted.

All of his predecessors, from Stalin onward, had had direct experience of ruling in the border areas and understood the mixture of force and tact necessary to keep them quiet. Gorbachev, however, lacking such experience, seems to have believed the official position developed under Brezhnev, namely that the nationalities had been fused into a genuine “Soviet people” committed to the “Union” as the vehicle for their economic development and international security. All they needed, therefore, was a little “restructuring,” as that term was understood by the “center.” In reality, however, the national republics were suffering from structural stagnation and institutional rigidities of the same sort that Gorbachev had run up against in the Party, compounded by ethnic grievances. And this problem, quite unexpectedly for the leadership, quickly became one of the three major factors—alongside economic failure and the eclipse of ideology—instrumental to bringing the system down. To explain this major problem a brief glance backward is necessary.

zh: 如前所述，在内战和1920年代初布尔什维克最初征服边疆地区之后，“中心”于1922年创建了一个“联邦制”苏联，实际上是单一制国家。
然而，其单一制性质被一种精心设计的民族制度化所掩盖，这种制度以族群—语言定义民族，并以领土为基础。

除俄罗斯外，每个“组成”共和国，以及较大共和国境内的各种“联系”共和国，都获得了自己的政治和文化机构，人员主要由新形成的本地精英充任，当然是在党的密切监督下运作。其目的是通过给予地方民族主义尊严来安抚它，同时将它收编用于建设社会主义。换言之，苏联民族政策是为国家建设和粗放经济增长而全面动员人口的另一方面。而且，借助镇压消除任何自主民族情绪，这套办法在斯大林和赫鲁晓夫治下的扩张年代，与制度其余部分运作得差不多一样好。例如，乌兹别克为全联盟生产棉花，阿塞拜疆生产石油，摩尔达维亚和格鲁吉亚贡献葡萄酒和烈酒，而俄罗斯供应钢铁。
en: As noted, following the original Bolshevik conquest of the border areas during the Civil War and the early 1920s, the “center” in 1922 had created a “federal” Soviet Union that was in fact a unitary state.
Its unitary character, however, was camouflaged by an elaborate institutionalization of nationality, defined in ethnic-linguistic terms, on a territorial basis.

Each “constituent” republic except Russia, as well as various “associated” republics within the larger ones, received its own political and cultural institutions staffed predominantly by newly formed native elites operating, of course, under the close supervision of the Party. The purpose of this was to appease local nationalism by dignifying it, and at the same time to coopt it for the purposes of building socialism. In other words, Soviet nationality policy was another aspect of the all-out mobilization of the population for state-building and extensive economic growth. And, with the aid of repression to eliminate any autonomous national sentiment, this worked about as well as the rest of the system during its decades of expansion under Stalin and Khrushchev. For example, Uzbekistan produced cotton for the entire Union, Azerbaijan produced oil, and Moldavia and Georgia contributed wines and spirits, while Russia supplied the steel.

〔译注〕俄罗斯联邦本身亦设有共和国级政治与文化机构；其党组织设置与其他加盟共和国不同，不应把原句理解为俄罗斯没有此类机构。

zh: “边缘”的问题总是比“中心”多。在最初军事征服边疆地区之后，由于民族主义力量重新出现——此时是在地方党内部——莫斯科不得不通过行政清洗定期进行政治“再征服”。在尤其敏感的乌克兰案例中——唯一一个其脱离本身就能摧毁联盟的共和国——斯大林至少进行了两次这样的清洗，赫鲁晓夫和勃列日涅夫各一次。
更重要的是，苏联政策一直无意中在以前不存在民族主义的地方制造民族主义。
en: But there were always more problems on the “periphery” than in the “center.” After the original military conquest of the border areas, Moscow periodically had to undertake a political “reconquest” via administrative purge because of the reappearance of nationalist forces, now within the local Party itself. In the especially sensitive case of Ukraine—the only republic whose defection by itself could destroy the Union—Stalin carried out such purges at least twice, and Khrushchev and Brezhnev once each.
Even more, Soviet policy all along was inadvertently creating nationalisms where they had not existed before.

zh: 大多数苏联共和国不是历史性民族，很少曾经拥有独立国家地位。格鲁吉亚和亚美尼亚是古老的民族实体，享受过各个独立时期。三个波罗的海国家从被淹没的农民群体中生长出来，这些农民群体直到19世纪末才形成民族意识，并在两次世界大战之间第一次独立。但乌克兰在其二战后边界内从未作为一个民族单位存在，也从未实现有效独立；乌克兰民族情感虽然非常真实，其最强基础在旧加利西亚，随着向东到哈尔科夫和顿巴斯或向南到敖德萨和克里米亚而逐渐减弱。在作者看来，苏维埃白俄罗斯作为民族实体的现实性比乌克兰更弱，而所有穆斯林共和国在苏维埃从旧突厥斯坦划出它们之前都从未是民族。然而，经过数十年以领土为基础的族群制度，这些实体都在成为拥有自己精英和制度化既得利益的民族共同体的路上。
en: Most of the Soviet republics were not historic nations, and very few had ever known independent statehood. Georgia and Armenia were ancient national entities that had enjoyed various periods of independence. The three Baltic states grew out of submerged peasantries that had developed national consciousness only at the end of the nineteenth century, and had first become independent between the two World Wars. But Ukraine, within its post-Second World War boundaries, had never existed as a national unit or achieved effective independence; Ukrainian national feeling, though very real, had its strongest base in old Galicia and weakened progressively as one moved east to Kharkov and the Donbas or south to Odessa and the Crimea. And Soviet Belorussia was even less of a reality than Ukraine, while none of the Muslim republics had ever been nations until the Soviets carved them out of old Turkestan, Yet after decades of territorially based ethnicity, these entities were all on their way to becoming national communities with their own elites and institutionalized vested interests.

zh: 此外，它们都是心怀不满的民族共同体。鉴于斯大林强加的分而治之边界，几乎所有共和国都在其他共和国内有本民族成员，在自己境内有来自相邻共和国民族的少数群体。几乎所有共和国都因工业化而有大量俄罗斯人定居其中；因为这些迁移是蓄意稀释领土同质性政策的一部分，以便创建与单一经济和单一党相配的单一苏联人民。然而，尽管民族文化抗议反复出现，只要经济能够支撑强大的中央国家，这个多民族帝国就保持稳定。因此勃列日涅夫可以在1970年代末轻易镇压公开的边疆民族主义，逮捕波罗的海国家、乌克兰和高加索所有主要民族异见者。
en: Furthermore, they were all aggrieved national communities. Given the divide-and-rule frontiers Stalin had imposed, almost all of these republics had minorities of their citizens in other republics, and minorities of neighboring ethnic groups within their own borders. Almost all had large numbers of Russians settled in their midst as a result of industrialization; for these migrations were part of a deliberate policy of diluting territorial homogeneity in order to create a single Soviet people to go with the unitary economy and the unitary Party. Yet, despite the recurrent appearance of national cultural protest, this multinational empire remained stable as long as the economy was able to support a strong central state. So Brezhnev could easily repress overt border nationalism in the late seventies by arresting all the leading national dissidents of the Baltic states. Ukraine, and the Caucasus.

zh: 尽管如此，停滞正像侵蚀制度其余部分一样侵蚀各共和国，原因相同。勃列日涅夫的“干部稳定”政策给每个共和国和地区提供了与整个党务机关一样抵制中央倡议的权力结构。尤其在穆斯林共和国，这一政策导致党实际上被族群酋长接管，他们像统治总督辖区一样控制自己的地区，并贿赂莫斯科使其纵容。与此同时，苏联式工业化造成的生态破坏被各共和国居民视为中央统治的恶果：特别是切尔诺贝利加速了乌克兰和白俄罗斯分离情绪的发展；地方机关很容易发现，支持这种情绪符合他们对抗莫斯科的利益。此外，经济衰退使资源更加稀缺，因而加剧了共和国之间以及共和国与中心之间对资源的竞争。这种不满积累的后果是一场日益壮大的争取地方自主权的运动，参与者把地方自主当作各民族共和国唯一合适的“改组”。而公开性第一次使谈论这一切成为可能，而不必过分担心报复。
en: Still, stagnation was undermining the republics just as it was eating, away at the rest of the system, and for the same reasons. Brezhnev’s policy of “stability of cadres” had provided each republic and region with a power structure as resistant to central initiative as was the Party apparat as a whole. Particularly in the Muslim republics, this policy had led to the virtual takeover of the Party by ethnic chieftains who controlled their regions as if they were satrapies, and who bribed Moscow into connivance. At the same time, the ecological depredations caused by Soviet-style industrialization were seen by the populations of the republics as the evil fruits of domination by the center: Chernobyl, in particular, accelerated the development of Ukrainian and Belorussian separatist sentiment; and the local apparats easily found it in their interests to espouse this sentiment against Moscow. Moreover, the decline of the economy made resources scarcer and therefore increased competition for them, both among the republics and between the republics and the center. The consequence of this accumulation of grievances was a growing movement for local control as the only appropriate “restructuring” for the national republics. And
for the first time made it possible to talk about all of this without undue fear of reprisal.

zh: 苏联民族政策的悲剧在于，它鼓励民族认同的发展，同时却只为由此激发的力量提供虚假的出路。没有采取任何措施让这些半民族对自己的事务拥有真正控制，或为真正的联邦关系铺路。结果，当有效自治的要求终于提出时，它只能采取中心与边缘利益正面冲突的形式。因改革而浮出水面的民族不满，并不像人们常说的那样，仅仅是被苏联统治长期淹没的传统民族主义的复兴；它们是一种新力量，即使不是由苏联权力创造，也是由它刺激起来的，然后又被苏联的控制压抑，最终激起强烈不满。如同苏联制度中的一切，国家单一结构的僵化排除了渐进过渡。因此，如果制度中其他任何东西要改革，联盟就无法保留。
en: The tragedy of Soviet nationality policy was that it encouraged the development of national identity while at the same time giving the energies thereby generated only a fraudulent outlet. Nothing was done to give these semi-nations any real control over their affairs, or to prepare the way for genuine federal relationships. As a consequence, when the demand for effective autonomy was at last raised, it could only take the form of a head-on clash of interests between the center and the periphery. The national discontents that came to the surface as a result of

did not: represent simply the resurgence of traditional nationalisms long submerged by Soviet rule, as has often been alleged; they were, rather, a new force stimulated if not created by Soviet power and then hobbled to the point of exasperation by Soviet control. As with everything else in the Soviet system, the rigidity of the state’s unitary structure ruled out an evolutionary transition. Thus the Union could not be preserved if anything else in the system were to be reformed.

zh: 戈尔巴乔夫1986年12月无意中跌入这一恶化局势。
作为他最初对整个机关攻击的一部分，他用一个诚实但外来的俄罗斯人取代了哈萨克斯坦腐败但本地的第一书记，后者也是政治局委员。回应是一场近乎起义的骚乱，抗议失去自治和在莫斯科最高层的代表权。结果，戈尔巴乔夫实际上不得不退让，任命一名哈萨克人担任第二书记；此外，在公开性下，对发生骚乱及随后退让的宣传让其他民族看到，他们也可以提出自己的要求。
en: Gorbachev inadvertently stumbled into this deteriorating situation in December 1986.

As a part of his initial attack on the apparat in general, he replaced the corrupt but native First Secretary of Kazakhstan, who was also a Politburo member, with an honest but imported Russian. The answer was a riot verging on revolt in protest against this loss of autonomy and of representation at the highest level in Moscow. As a result, Gorbachev in effect had to back down by appointing a Kazakh Second Secretary; moreover, under
, the publicity given to the fact that there had been a riot followed by a retreat showed other nationalities that they, too, might press their demands.

zh: 次年年初，改革遭遇一场“道德切尔诺贝利”，正如一位苏联领导人所称，即纳戈尔内卡拉巴赫

——阿塞拜疆境内的亚美尼亚飞地。这个地区人口80%是亚美尼亚人，1923年被斯大林划给阿塞拜疆，因为当时他更需要安抚土耳其人而非亚美尼亚人的意见。然而随着“改组”的到来，该地区的亚美尼亚人寻求通过申请改变地位来纠正这一长期不满。申请被拒后，人群在该地区首府斯捷潘纳克特和亚美尼亚共和国首都埃里温上街示威；他们的口号是“卡拉巴赫是改革的试金石”。1988年2月，这些示威导致纳戈尔内卡拉巴赫的亚美尼亚人与阿塞拜疆人武装冲突，冲突又在阿塞拜疆首都巴库附近的苏姆盖特引发针对亚美尼亚人的屠杀。随后多达一百万人在埃里温列宁广场抗议屠杀，由“卡拉巴赫委员会”领导；亚美尼亚党实际上倒向民族运动，颠倒了政权为这类人民阵线设计的公式。
en: At the beginning of the next year
was struck by a “moral Chernobyl,” as one Soviet leader put it, in the form of Nagornyi Karabakh,

an Armenian enclave in Azerbaijan. This region, whose population was 80 percent Armenian, had been assigned by Stalin to Azerbaijan in 1923, because at the time he had more need to propitiate Turkish than Armenian opinion. With the coming of “restructuring,” however, the Armenians of the region sought to redress this long-standing grievance by petitioning for a change in status. When the petition was rejected, crowds took to the streets in demonstrations, both in the region’s capital, Stepanakert, and in the capital of the Armenian republic, Erivan; their slogan was “Karabakh is the test of

.” In February 1988, these demonstrations led to armed clashes with Azerbaijani in Nagornyi Karabakh, and these clashes prompted a pogrom against Armenians in Sumgait, near the Azerbaijani capital of Baku. Crowds of up to a million then protested the pogrom on Lenin Square in Erivan under the leadership of the “Kara-bakh Committee,” and the Armenian Party in effect went over to the national movement in an inversion of the regime’s intended formula for such Popular Fronts.

zh: 在这次冲突最初爆发之后，莫斯科不愿考虑任何边界变更，害怕在其他共和国引发连锁反应，于是拖延时间，天真地希望情绪会冷却、问题会消失。各种给予卡拉巴赫有限特殊地位的方案都尝试过并失败了。唯一结果是，此前传统上因需要莫斯科保护以对抗土耳其人而安于苏联监护的亚美尼亚人，现在变成反苏并一心追求独立。虽然亚美尼亚由苏联军队维持治安，实际上一个“双重政权”已经出现。
en: After this first explosion, Moscow, unwilling to contemplate any border changes for fear of producing a chain reaction in other republics, played for time in the uninformed hope that passions would cool and the problem would go away. Various schemes for giving Karabakh a limited special status were tried and failed. The only result was that the Armenians, hitherto traditionally reconciled to Soviet tutelage because of their need for Moscow’s protection against the Turks, now became anti-Soviet and bent on independence. Although Armenia was policed by Soviet troops, in fact a regime of “dual power” had come into existence.

zh: 与此同时，亚美尼亚收回纳戈尔内卡拉巴赫的努力导致阿塞拜疆出现一个具有民族意识的人民阵线。起初该阵线只针对阿塞拜疆的邻国，但随着莫斯科在争议领土地位上似乎动摇，它也转向反对“俄罗斯人”。由于两个高加索共和国都无法从中心获得满足，双方都把事务掌握在自己手中；在1989年过程中，它们陷入一场低烈度战争。阿塞拜疆对亚美尼亚实施铁路封锁，各共和国国民带着武器——偶尔甚至带着直升机——从苏军开小差。仿佛中央权威的瓦解还不够，俄罗斯的母亲们开始示威，反对苏军拿她们的“孩子们”冒险去维持“野蛮山民”之间的秩序。
en: At the same time, the Armenian efforts to retrieve Nagornyi Karabakh had led to the emergence of a nationally minded Popular Front in Azerbaijan. At first the Front was directed only against Azerbaijan’s neighbors, but, as Moscow appeared to waver on the status of the disputed territory, it was turned against the “Russians” as well. Because neither Caucasian republic could obtain satisfaction from the center, both took matters into their own hands; and, during the course of 1989, they became locked in a low-grade war. Azerbaijan imposed a rail blockade on Armenia, and nationals of each republic deserted from the Soviet army with their weapons—and occasionally even with helicopters. As if this were not enough in the way of disintegration of central authority, mothers in Russia took to demonstrating against the Soviet army’s risking their “boys” to keep order among the “wild mountaineers.”

zh: 最后，1989年间，族群冲突蔓延到山区其余地方。阿布哈兹联系共和国——斯大林为制造一个更小、更难以生存的格鲁吉亚而创建——脱离格鲁吉亚的运动，在改革下导致格鲁吉亚民族主义高涨。但由此产生的格鲁吉亚人民阵线很快把敌意从阿布哈兹人转向他们所谓的后台苏联中心；到1989年4月，情绪激动的人群在第比利斯示威，要求实现正成为其真正目标的独立。地方当局惊恐，可能在中心纵容下动用军队对付人群：4月9日，约一百人在改革年代第一次流血中丧生。虽然由此恢复了表面秩序，实际上又制造了一个双重权力区。于是，在1988—1989年过程中，三个高加索共和国都已远远超出改革，走向联盟的解体。
en: Finally, during 1989, ethnic conflict spread to the rest of the mountain area. A movement for the secession from Georgia of the Abkhazian Associated Republic (created by Stalin in order to produce a smaller and less viable Georgia) led, under

, to an upsurge of Georgian nationalism. But the resulting Georgian Popular Front soon transferred its animus from the Abkhazians to their alleged sponsor, the Soviet center; and by April 1989 emotional crowds were demonstrating in Tbilisi for what was becoming their real aim, independence. The local authorities took fright, and with the probable connivance of the center, used the army against the crowds: On April 9, some one hundred persons were killed in the first bloodshed of the
years. Although a semblance of order was thereby restored, in fact another zone of dual power had been created. Thus, in the course of 1988-1989 all three Caucasian republics had gone far beyond
and towards the breakup of the Union.

zh: 在这同一两年里，三个波罗的海国家也展开另一场民族解放运动，不过这里是以严格合法和非暴力的方式进行的。斯大林的遗产再次回来纠缠他的继承人。波罗的海人的策略是主张，1939年《莫洛托夫-里宾特洛甫条约》的秘密议定书把他们的共和国划给苏联，从来就是非法的；因此他们只是分阶段收回一项在国际法下仍被承认的独立。1988年4月，爱沙尼亚自由派知识分子与党内某些分子组成人民阵线，为共和国“主权”而努力；这标志着该口号第一次出现在非正式改革的词汇中。当6月党代表会议未对其要求给予任何注意时，爱沙尼亚党把主动权丢给了非党盟友；11月，激进化的爱沙尼亚议会通过投票赋予共和国法律高于苏联法律的效力，从而实施了其主权要求。
en: During these same two years another movement of national liberation opened up in the three Baltic states, though here this occurred in a scrupulously legalistic and nonviolent manner. Once again, the legacy of Stalin came home to haunt his heirs. The Balts’ tactic was to argue that the secret protocols to the Molotov-Ribbentrop Pact of 1939, which had awarded their republics to the Soviet Union, had never been legal; as a consequence they were only reclaiming, by stages, an independence still recognized under international law. In April 1988, therefore, liberal intellectuals in Estonia formed a Popular Front with certain elements of the Party to work for republic “sovereignty”; this marked the first appearance of that slogan in the lexicon of informal

. When the Party Conference in June failed to pay any attention to its demands, the Estonian Party lost the initiative to its non-Party allies; and in November a radicalized Estonian Parliament implemented its demand for sovereignty by voting to give republic laws precedence over Soviet laws.

zh: 这种通过非暴力方式否定联盟权威的做法，比纳戈尔内卡拉巴赫更难让戈尔巴乔夫应付：如果改革要保持可信，他不能使用武力；但如果中央权威要保持真实，他也不能让爱沙尼亚如此无礼却不受约束。但甚至在爱沙尼亚人采取这一步骤之前，拉脱维亚人和立陶宛人也已组成自己的人民阵线（在立陶宛称为萨尤迪斯），以争取主权。此外，到1989年初，三个阵线都公开要求正式谴责1939年条约，这也是在说主权实际上意味着独立。此外，这场波罗的海运动已经开始在乌克兰西部的利沃夫得到呼应，那里也因该条约而成为苏联的一部分。
en: This nonviolent nullification of Union authority was even harder for Gorbachev to deal with than was Nagornyi Karabakh: he could not use force if

were to remain credible, yet he could not let Estonia get away with its insolence if central authority were to remain real. But even before the Estonians had taken this step, the Latvians and Lithuanians had also formed their own Popular Fronts (in Lithuania, it was called Sajudis) to press for sovereignty. Moreover, by early 1989 all three Fronts were openly demanding formal denunciation of the 1939 Pact, which was also a way of saying that sovereignty in fact meant independence. In addition, this Baltic agitation was already beginning to find an echo in Lvov, or Lviv, in western Ukraine, which had also become Soviet: because of the Pact.

zh: 于是，在1989年初，正当戈尔巴乔夫最伟大的改革——苏维埃民主化——即将生效时，他先前的改革——公开性——已经使新改革想要挽救的制度的大部分失去合法性。民主化现在将允许一个初生的公民社会组织起来，从单纯改革走向针对制度的渐进革命。
en: Thus in early 1989, just when Gorbachev’s greatest reform—democratization of the soviets—was about to take effect, his previous reform,

, had already delegitimized much of the system the new reform was intended to salvage. Democratization would now permit a nascent civil society to organize and to move from mere reform to creeping revolution against the system.
